Every participant must give a gift to exactly one person and receive a gift from exactly one person. A person cannot give a gift to themselves, and two people cannot give gifts directly to each other. Keep shuffling and evaluating the pairs until all conditions are met. Return an array of arrays, where each inner array contains two strings representing the giver and the receiver. For example, given four names, the output is an array of four pairings where no circular two-person loops exist.

title: Seismograph Spike Detector
spec: Write a function `detect(readings, factor)` that receives an array of amplitude measurements as numbers and a multiplier threshold. Iterate through the measurements and maintain a rolling average of the last five values. A significant event begins when the current reading is greater than the rolling average multiplied by the threshold factor. The event ends when the reading drops back below the rolling average. Keep track of the starting index of each event. Return an array of integers representing the starting indices of all detected events. For example, if a spike occurs at the tenth measurement that exceeds the historical average times the factor, the number ten is added to the results.

title: Text Wrapping Engine
spec: Implement a function `wrap(text, width)` that takes a long string of words and an integer representing the maximum line width. Split the text into individual words and construct lines one by one. Add words to the current line, separated by spaces, until adding another word would exceed the maximum width. When a line becomes full, push it to an array of lines and begin a new line. If a single word is longer than the width, it must be placed on its own line. Return an array of strings where each string is a properly wrapped line. For example, given a paragraph and a width of fifteen, the output is an array of tightly packed strings.

title: Dart Match Scorer
spec: Create a function `score(throws, target)` that evaluates a sequence of dart throws for two alternating players. The first argument is an array of numeric point values, and the second is the starting score for both players. Players take turns throwing three darts at a time, subtracting the points from their respective remaining totals. If a throw causes a player's score to drop below zero, that throw is invalid, their turn ends immediately, and their score resets to what it was at the start of that turn. The first player to reach exactly zero wins. Return an array containing the index of the winning player as an integer and a boolean flag indicating if the match ended in a victory or remained unfinished.

title: Disk Defragmenter Simulation
spec: Design a function `defragment(files, blocks)` that simulates organizing data. The first array contains integers representing the sizes of files in memory. The second array contains zeros and ones representing free and occupied storage blocks respectively. Find the earliest continuous sequence of free blocks that can fit the first file, and mark those blocks as occupied. Continue this process for each file in order. If a file cannot fit anywhere, skip it and try the next one. Return an array of integers representing the final state of the storage blocks. For example, placing a file of size two into an empty disk will turn the first two zeros into ones.

title: Cryptography Caesar Cipher
spec: Write a function `encrypt(message, shift)` that applies a classic letter substitution cipher to a string. Iterate through each character of the message. If the character is a standard alphabetical letter, shift it forward in the alphabet by the numeric shift amount, wrapping around from the end of the alphabet back to the beginning. Preserve the uppercase or lowercase formatting of the original letter. Non-alphabetical characters like punctuation or numbers should be left unchanged. Return the newly encrypted string. For example, shifting the word apple by one produces bqqmf.

title: Roman Numeral Converter
spec: Implement a function `romanize(values)` that translates an array of standard integers into traditional symbols. For each integer, build a string by repeatedly subtracting the largest possible Roman numeral value from the integer and appending the corresponding letter combinations to a temporary string. Handle all standard subtractive notation cases such as four, nine, forty, and ninety. If a number is less than one or greater than three thousand nine hundred ninety nine, append an empty string instead. Return an array of strings containing the converted numerals. For example, passing an array with the number fourteen returns an array containing the string ten followed by one and five.

title: Word Frequency Histogram
spec: Create a function `tabulate(text)` that takes a string of prose, removes all punctuation, and converts all letters to lowercase. Split the sanitized string into individual words and count how many times each unique word appears. Convert these counts into an array of paired elements, where each pair is an array containing the word as a string and its frequency as an integer. Sort this outer array in descending order based on the frequency counts. If two words have the same frequency, sort them alphabetically. Return the sorted array of arrays. For example, the sentence the cat and the dog returns the pair for the at the top with a count of two.

title: Sudoku Grid Validator
spec: Design a function `validate(grid)` that checks the correctness of a completed number puzzle. The input is an array of nine arrays, each containing nine integers from one to nine. Check every horizontal row to ensure it contains no duplicate numbers. Check every vertical column for the same condition. Finally, check all nine three by three subgrids to ensure they also contain no duplicates. If any row, column, or subgrid is invalid, stop checking and prepare a negative result. Return a boolean indicating whether the entire grid is a perfectly valid solution. For example, a mathematically sound board returns true.

title: Packet Loss Reconstructor
spec: Write a function `reconstruct(packets, placeholder)` that reassembles an out of order data transmission. The first input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains an integer sequence number and a string payload. Sort the incoming packets by their sequence numbers. Determine the starting and ending sequence numbers. Construct a new array of strings containing the payloads in order. If any sequence number in the continuous range is missing from the input, insert the string placeholder in that exact position. Return the continuous array of strings. For example, missing the second sequence replaces the second output element with the placeholder.

title: Vowel Shift Encryption
spec: Implement a function `shift(phrase)` that alters a sentence by rotating only its vowels. Traverse the string and collect all vowels into an array while preserving their original order and case. Shift the collected vowels cyclically by moving the last vowel to the front of the array. Traverse the original string a second time, building a new string where consonants are kept in place, but each vowel is replaced by the next available shifted vowel from the array. Return the newly built string. For example, shifting the word hello moves the only two vowels around, replacing the first with the second and the second with the first.

title: Palindrome Sentence Checker
spec: Create a function `palindromes(phrases)` that analyzes an array of text phrases. For each phrase, create a sanitized version by stripping out all spaces and punctuation, and converting all remaining characters to lowercase. Check if this sanitized string reads identically forwards and backwards. Keep a count of how many phrases satisfy this condition. Return an array containing two elements: the total count of valid palindromes as an integer, and an array of booleans mapped to the original phrases indicating their individual results. For example, the phrase race car evaluates to true.

title: Genetic Sequence Matcher
spec: Design a function `sequence(dna, motif)` that locates occurrences of a small genetic pattern within a longer strand. Both inputs are strings of nucleotide letters. Slide a window the size of the motif across the longer strand. For each position, compare the characters of the window to the motif. Count the number of mismatched characters. If the mismatch count is less than or equal to one, the current starting index is considered a valid match. Collect all valid starting indices. Return an array of integers representing the starting locations. For example, matching a motif against an identical strand returns an array containing the number zero.

title: Disk Usage Hierarchy
spec: Write a function `calculate(paths, sizes)` that aggregates file sizes by their top level directories. The first input is an array of strings representing file paths separated by slashes. The second input is an array of integers representing the byte size of each file. Extract the first directory name from each path. Accumulate the total size for each unique top level directory. Build an array of paired items, where each pair is an array containing the directory name as a string and its total size as an integer. Return this array of arrays. For example, two files within the documents folder will result in a single pair summing their sizes.

title: Hexadecimal Color Gradients
spec: Implement a function `gradient(start, end, steps)` that generates a smooth transition between two colors. Parse the two six character strings into their red, green, and blue numerical components. Calculate the numerical difference for each color channel between the start and end values. Divide this difference by the number of steps to find the increment per step. Loop through the requested number of steps, adding the increment to the current color values, and convert the new numbers back into rounded hexadecimal strings. Return an array of strings representing the color sequence. For example, bridging black and white with three steps yields dark grey and light grey in between.

title: Snake Game Simulator
spec: Create a function `slither(snake, apple, direction, size)` that calculates the next frame of a grid based game. The snake is an array of coordinate pairs, where the first pair is the head. Calculate the new head position by moving one space based on the string direction provided. Check if the new head goes outside the grid size or intersects with any existing body segments. If it does, the game is lost. If the new head matches the apple coordinate, the snake grows, so keep all previous segments. Otherwise, remove the tail segment. Return an array containing a boolean representing survival, and the updated snake array of arrays.

title: Run Length Encoding Compression
spec: Design a function `compress(data)` that shortens a string by grouping repeating adjacent characters. Iterate through the characters of the string. Keep a running tally of how many times the current character has appeared consecutively. When a different character is encountered, append the previous character and its numeric tally to a result string, then reset the tally to one. After processing the entire string, compare the length of the newly generated string to the original input. Return the shorter of the two strings. For example, three consecutive letter a characters become the letter a followed by the number three.

title: Maze Solver Breadth First
spec: Write a function `navigate(maze)` that finds the shortest exit path. The input is an array of strings where each character represents a wall, an open path, the starting point, or the exit. Use an array to act as a queue of coordinates to visit, and maintain a historical record of visited coordinates. For each coordinate, explore adjacent open paths that have not yet been visited, tracking the sequence of moves that led there. Stop searching when the exit character is found. Return an array of coordinate arrays representing the shortest path from start to finish. If no path exists, return an empty array.

title: Bounding Box Collisions
spec: Implement a function `intersect(rectangles)` that checks a collection of shapes for overlaps. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains four integers representing the horizontal position, vertical position, width, and height. Compare every unique pair of shapes to see if their boundaries overlap on both axes. Two shapes collide if one's left edge is entirely past the other's right edge, or if one's top edge is entirely below the other's bottom edge. Collect the indices of all colliding pairs. Return an array of arrays, where each inner array contains two integers representing the overlapping indices.

title: Pascal Triangle Generator
spec: Create a function `generate(rows)` that builds a classic mathematical structure. The input is an integer dictating how many horizontal levels to compute. Start with an initial row containing just the number one. For each subsequent row, place a one at the beginning and the end. Fill the interior numbers by looking at the previous row and adding together the adjacent numbers located directly above and to the left and right. Accumulate all constructed rows into a master list. Return an array of arrays of integers. For example, requesting three levels returns an array with a first level of one, a second level of one and one, and a third level of one, two, and one.

title: Checkers Valid Jumps
spec: Design a function `jumps(board, position)` that identifies legal capturing moves on a grid. The first input is an array of arrays populated with integers representing empty spaces, player pieces, and opponent pieces. The second input is an array of two integers for the starting coordinates. Examine the four diagonal directions from the starting point. A valid jump requires an opponent piece directly adjacent in the diagonal direction, followed by an empty space immediately behind it. Verify that neither coordinate falls outside the grid boundaries. Return an array of arrays containing the ending coordinates for all valid jumps. For example, an isolated piece in the center might return four possible landing spots.

title: Text Diffing Algorithm
spec: Write a function `compare(original, revised)` that analyzes changes between two documents. Both inputs are arrays of strings representing individual lines. Compare the elements sequentially. If the lines are identical, record the line with a status of unchanged. If a line is present in the first array but not in the second, record it as deleted. If a line appears in the second array but not the first, record it as added. Keep track of current positions in both arrays and look ahead up to three lines to resynchronize after an addition or deletion. Return an array of arrays containing a status string and the line content string.

title: Email Thread Unroller
spec: Write a function `unroll` that takes an array of formatted email strings. Each string starts with a depth indicator formed by a series of greater than symbols, followed by a space, and then the message text. Structure the code as a small module with separate helper functions for extracting the depth and text, and for checking the direct reply status. The main function must count the number of greater than symbols to determine the reply depth. It should skip any message that contains the word unsubscribe in lowercase. For the remaining messages, keep track of whether the message is a direct reply, which is true if the depth is exactly one. Return an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the extracted message text, the numerical depth, and a boolean indicating if it is a direct reply. Example input: an array containing greater than symbol hello, and greater than greater than symbol hi there. Expected output: an array containing an inner array with hello, one, true, and another inner array with hi there, two, false.

title: Sensor Calibration Checker
spec: Write a function `calibrate` that takes an array of numerical sensor readings and a text string representing the sensor model. Structure the solution as a small module with helper functions for filtering readings and computing averages. The main process must iterate through the readings and discard any negative values. It calculates the average of the valid readings using a helper. It then determines if the sensor is reliable, which is true if the average is between ninety and one hundred and ten inclusive, and the sensor model string starts with the letters cal. Return an array containing the average as a number, the reliability status as a boolean, and a status string which is either passed or failed based on the reliability. Example input: an array of ninety five, negative ten, one hundred, and the model string calibration unit. Expected output: an array with ninety seven point five, true, and passed.

title: Paint Mixture Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize` that takes an array of paint color ratios as numbers, and a string representing the target color name. Use a modular approach with separate helper functions to apply loss factors and sum volumes. The main logic loops through the ratios and applies a loss factor by multiplying each ratio by zero point nine. It calculates the total volume of the adjusted ratios. A boolean flag should be set to true if the total volume exceeds fifty. If the total volume is sufficient, append the word ready to the target color name; otherwise, append the word insufficient. Return an array containing the new string, the total volume number, and the boolean flag. Example input: an array of twenty, thirty, ten, and the string blue. Expected output: an array with blue ready, fifty four, true.

title: Conveyor Belt Sorter
spec: Write a function `sort` that receives an array of item weights and a string for the destination zone. Implement this as a small module with helper functions for isolating heavy items and determining the load status. The process iterates over the weights, isolating those that are heavier than twenty. For these heavy items, it sums their weights and counts how many there are. It defines a boolean variable indicating if the conveyor is overloaded, which is true if the sum is greater than two hundred or the count is greater than five. The destination string is modified by appending either blocked or active based on the overloaded status. The function returns an array with the modified destination string, the total heavy weight, and the overloaded boolean. Example input: array of ten, twenty five, thirty, and the string north. Expected output: array with north active, fifty five, false.

title: Invoice Reminder Generator
spec: Write a function `remind` that accepts an array of past due amounts as numbers and a string representing the client name. Divide the work into helper functions for summing amounts and constructing messages. The main function must calculate the total past due amount by summing all positive numbers in the array. It computes a boolean status representing whether the account is suspended, which is true if the total is over five hundred. If suspended, it constructs a warning message combining the client name and the phrase account locked; otherwise it combines the client name and please pay. Return an array containing the constructed message string, the total amount as a number, and the suspension boolean. Example input: array of one hundred, two hundred, and the string alpha corp. Expected output: array with alpha corp please pay, three hundred, false.

title: Classroom Attendance Grader
spec: Write a function `grade` that takes an array of daily attendance minutes as numbers and a string for the student identifier. Create a small module with helper functions for filtering valid days and calculating averages. The logic should filter out any days where the attendance was less than ten minutes. The remaining valid minutes are averaged. A boolean variable is created to represent perfect standing, which is true if the average is at least forty five. The student identifier string is appended with either honors or standard based on this standing. The function should return an array holding the modified student identifier string, the calculated average number, and the perfect standing boolean. Example input: array of fifty, five, forty, and the string student a. Expected output: array with student a honors, forty five, true.

title: Crop Yield Forecaster
spec: Write a function `forecast` that takes an array of weekly rainfall measurements in millimeters and a string denoting the crop type. Organize the solution using helper functions for data cleaning and condition evaluation. The algorithm removes any rainfall values that are exactly zero. It then calculates the sum of the remaining rainfall. A boolean indicator should be evaluated to true if the total rainfall is between one hundred and two hundred. The crop type string is updated by appending the word optimal if the indicator is true, or sub-optimal if false. Return an array containing the updated crop string, the total rainfall number, and the boolean indicator. Example input: array of fifty, zero, sixty, and the string wheat. Expected output: array with wheat optimal, one hundred ten, true.

title: Shipment Tracker Validations
spec: Write a function `validate` that takes an array of transit times in hours and a string containing the courier code. Build a modular script with helpers for filtering anomalies and computing delays. The function ignores any transit times over one hundred hours as anomalies. It sums the valid transit times to find the total journey duration. A boolean is declared to track if the delivery is delayed, which becomes true if the total duration is greater than forty eight hours. Depending on the delayed status, the courier code string is concatenated with either late or on time. Return an array containing the final courier string, the total duration number, and the delayed boolean. Example input: array of twenty, thirty, one hundred fifty, and the string fast track. Expected output: array with fast track late, fifty, true.

title: Network Signal Strength Processor
spec: Write a function `process` that takes an array of signal strengths and a string indicating the router model. Break the logic down into helper functions for filtering noise and finding the maximum value. The routine should filter the strengths to keep only values above ten. It then determines the maximum signal strength from the filtered valid list. It defines a boolean showing if the connection is excellent, which evaluates to true if the maximum strength is above eighty. The router model string gets the suffix pro added if the connection is excellent, or basic otherwise. The function returns an array with the updated model string, the maximum strength number, and the excellent connection boolean. Example input: array of five, fifty, eighty five, and the string net core. Expected output: array with net core pro, eighty five, true.

title: Payroll Bonus Distributor
spec: Write a function `distribute` that takes an array of employee performance scores as numbers and a string for the department name. Structure the code as a small module with separate functions to filter scores and format department names. The logic filters out scores below fifty. It calculates the total bonus pool by multiplying the length of the filtered scores array by one hundred. A boolean variable checks if the department is a high achiever, which is true if the bonus pool exceeds five hundred. The department name string is updated by adding a star suffix if the department is a high achiever. Return an array containing the updated department string, the bonus pool number, and the high achiever boolean. Example input: array of sixty, forty, seventy, and the string sales. Expected output: array with sales, two hundred, false.

title: Wind Turbine Output Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate` that accepts an array of daily megawatt outputs and a string for the turbine location. Use small helper functions to handle filtering and peak detection. The function discards any outputs that are below five. It finds the highest output value among the valid days. A boolean is created to represent peak efficiency, which is true if the highest output is greater than fifty. The location string is modified by appending the phrase peak mode if the efficiency is true, or normal mode otherwise. Return an array with the modified location string, the highest output number, and the boolean flag. Example input: array of two, ten, sixty, and the string north hill. Expected output: array with north hill peak mode, sixty, true.

title: Application Memory Profiler
spec: Write a function `profile` that takes an array of memory usage samples in megabytes and a string representing the process name. Create a modular script with helpers for filtering out low memory samples and calculating averages. The function filters out samples that are less than ten megabytes. It computes the average of the valid memory samples. A boolean memory leak warning is set to true if the average is above one thousand megabytes. The process name string is prepended with the word warning if the leak warning is true, or stable otherwise. Return an array containing the prepended process string, the average memory number, and the warning boolean. Example input: array of five, two thousand, two thousand, and the string background worker. Expected output: array with warning background worker, two thousand, true.

title: Delivery Route Distance Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate` that receives an array of segment distances in miles and a string for the driver name. Design the solution with separate helper functions for data validation and distance aggregation. The function removes any distances that are negative, assuming they are logged errors. It then calculates the total distance of all valid segments. A boolean indicating a long haul is evaluated to true if the total distance is fifty or more. The driver name string has the word local or long appended depending on the long haul boolean. The function returns an array containing the updated driver string, the total distance number, and the long haul boolean. Example input: array of twenty, negative five, thirty, and the string john. Expected output: array with john long, fifty, true.

title: Fasting Period Tracker
spec: Write a function `track` that takes an array of fasting hours over a week and a string for the participant name. Break the procedure into smaller helper functions for validating fasting periods and assessing ketosis state. The routine should exclude any periods less than twelve hours. It sums the remaining valid hours to find the total deep fasting time. A boolean indicating ketosis achieved is set to true if the total time is over forty hours. The participant name string is extended by adding the word success if ketosis is achieved, or try again otherwise. Return an array with the extended participant string, the total fasting number, and the ketosis boolean. Example input: array of ten, sixteen, eighteen, and the string alice. Expected output: array with alice try again, thirty four, false.

title: Website Click Traffic Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze` that receives an array of hourly click counts and a string for the webpage path. Use a modular approach with specific helper functions to clean the data and find peak hours. The algorithm filters out hours with zero clicks. It finds the maximum clicks in a single hour from the remaining data. A boolean representing a viral trend is set to true if the maximum clicks exceed one thousand. The webpage path string is wrapped in exclamation marks if the viral trend is true. The function returns an array with the modified path string, the maximum click number, and the viral trend boolean. Example input: array of zero, five hundred, twelve hundred, and the string home page. Expected output: array with exclamation home page exclamation, twelve hundred, true.

title: Solar Flare Intensity Processor
spec: Write a function `process` that takes an array of flare intensity numbers and a string for the satellite identifier. Organize the code into a small module using helpers for filtering data and computing safe averages. The function drops any intensity below fifty. It averages the remaining high intensity values. A boolean danger alert is set to true if the average is above two hundred. The satellite identifier string is updated by appending safe or danger based on the alert boolean. Return an array containing the new satellite string, the average intensity number, and the danger alert boolean. Example input: array of twenty, one hundred, three hundred, and the string sat one. Expected output: array with sat one safe, two hundred, false.

title: Ferris Wheel Load Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance` that accepts an array of passenger weights and a string for the cabin color. Implement this requirement using helper functions for filtering lightweight cargo and summarizing the total weight. The function filters out weights below twenty. It calculates the total weight of the valid passengers. A boolean representing capacity reached is set to true if the total weight is over three hundred. The cabin color string is modified by adding the word full if capacity is reached, or boarding otherwise. Return an array with the updated cabin string, the total weight number, and the capacity boolean. Example input: array of fifteen, one hundred, two hundred ten, and the string red. Expected output: array with red full, three hundred ten, true.

title: Sound Wave Peak Detector
spec: Write a function `detect` that takes an array of decibel measurements and a string for the audio track name. Compose a modular solution using helpers for extracting valid noise ranges and isolating the peak level. The algorithm filters out any measurements below thirty decibels as background noise. It identifies the peak decibel level from the remaining measurements. A boolean indicating hearing damage risk is evaluated to true if the peak is above eighty five decibels. The track name string gets the word loud appended if the risk is true. Return an array containing the modified track string, the peak decibel number, and the risk boolean. Example input: array of twenty, seventy, ninety, and the string rock song. Expected output: array with rock song loud, ninety, true.

title: Online Multiplayer Matchmaker
spec: Write a function `matchmake` that receives an array of player skill ratings as numbers and a string for the server region. Construct a small module with separate functions to process ratings and determine the lobby type. The logic discards any skill ratings below one thousand. It calculates the average skill rating of the valid players. A boolean indicating a competitive lobby is set to true if the average is greater than two thousand. The region string is updated by prepending the word ranked if it is a competitive lobby, or casual otherwise. The function returns an array with the updated region string, the average rating number, and the competitive boolean. Example input: array of five hundred, fifteen hundred, twenty five hundred, and the string europe. Expected output: array with casual europe, two thousand, false.

title: Video Streaming Buffering
spec: Write a function `buffer` that accepts an array of download speeds in kilobits per second and a string for the video resolution. Create helper functions to handle the speed filtering and minimum speed identification. The routine filters out speeds less than one hundred. It determines the minimum download speed from the valid speeds. A boolean representing smooth playback is set to true if the minimum speed is at least five hundred. The resolution string is appended with either hd ready or buffering based on the smooth playback boolean. Return an array containing the appended resolution string, the minimum speed number, and the playback boolean. Example input: array of fifty, six hundred, eight hundred, and the string ten eighty p. Expected output: array with ten eighty p hd ready, six hundred, true.

title: Athlete Heart Recovery Rate
spec: Write a function `recover` that takes an array of heart rate beats per minute taken at one minute intervals and a string for the athlete name. Build the solution using separate helper functions for data cleansing and calculating the recovery drop. The function filters out any rates below sixty. It calculates the drop between the first valid rate and the last valid rate. A boolean indicating excellent recovery is set to true if the drop is greater than thirty beats. The athlete name string is updated by adding the phrase fit or improving depending on the recovery boolean. The function returns an array with the updated athlete string, the calculated drop number, and the recovery boolean. Example input: array of fifty, one hundred fifty, one hundred, and the string david. Expected output: array with david fit, fifty, true.

title: Remote Server Uptime Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate` that receives an array of daily uptime percentages as numbers and a string for the data center name. Structure the logic into small helper functions to handle filtering downtime and averaging uptime. The algorithm ignores any days with exactly zero percent uptime. It computes the average uptime from the remaining days. A boolean indicating a reliable server is set to true if the average is ninety nine or higher. The data center string is modified by appending premium if the server is reliable, or standard otherwise. Return an array with the modified data center string, the average uptime number, and the reliable boolean. Example input: array of zero, ninety nine, ninety nine, and the string east coast. Expected output: array with east coast premium, ninety nine, true.

title: Sailing Regatta Wind Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze` that accepts an array of wind speeds in knots and a string for the boat class. Organize the code with helper functions for cleaning wind data and identifying the maximum gust. The logic removes any wind speeds under five knots as negligible. It finds the maximum wind speed from the valid entries. A boolean representing a gale warning is set to true if the maximum speed exceeds thirty knots. The boat class string is prepended with the word warning if the gale warning is true, or clear otherwise. Return an array containing the prepended boat string, the maximum wind speed number, and the gale warning boolean. Example input: array of two, twenty, thirty five, and the string catamaran. Expected output: array with warning catamaran, thirty five, true.

title: Code Repository Commit Counter
spec: Write a function `count` that takes an array of daily commit counts as numbers and a string for the developer username. Split the logic into smaller helper functions for removing inactive days and summing the commits. The routine filters out weekend days represented by zero commits. It calculates the total number of commits from the valid days. A boolean indicating highly active is set to true if the total commits are fifty or more. The username string is updated by adding the suffix pro if the highly active boolean is true. The function returns an array with the updated username string, the total commit number, and the highly active boolean. Example input: array of zero, ten, twenty, twenty five, and the string coder nine. Expected output: array with coder nine pro, fifty five, true.

title: Ceramic Tile Glaze Checker
spec: Write a function `check` that receives an array of glaze thickness measurements in millimeters and a string for the tile pattern. Formulate the script as a module with helper functions for extracting valid measurements and calculating the mean. The algorithm discards any measurements that are exactly zero. It averages the remaining thickness values. A boolean indicating pass quality is set to true if the average is between two and four inclusive. The tile pattern string is appended with either approved or rejected based on the pass quality boolean. Return an array containing the appended pattern string, the average thickness number, and the pass quality boolean. Example input: array of zero, three, five, and the string mosaic. Expected output: array with mosaic approved, four, true.

title: Anagram Group Size Analyzer
spec: Write a function called `analyze(words, threshold)`. The function should find all groups of words that are anagrams of each other. It must return an array containing two numbers: the number of anagram groups that have a size greater than or equal to the threshold, and the size of the largest anagram group. For example, given ["bat", "tab", "cat", "act", "mac"] and threshold 2, the output should be [2, 2].

title: Pallet Weight Balancer
spec: Implement a function called `balance(cargo, limit)`. Each item is an array with an identifier string and a weight number. The items must be placed onto pallets sequentially. An item is added to the current pallet if its weight does not cause the pallet's total weight to exceed the limit. If it does, a new pallet is started with this item. The function must return an array containing two numbers: the total number of pallets used, and the weight of the heaviest pallet. For example, given [["box1", 40], ["box2", 50], ["box3", 20]] and limit 80, the output is [2, 70].

title: Municipal Election Tally
spec: Write a function called `tally(ballots)`. Each ballot is an array containing a candidate name string, a district name string, and a validity boolean. If the validity is false, the ballot is discarded. The function must count the valid votes for each candidate across all districts. It should return an array containing two elements: the name of the winning candidate as a string (resolving ties alphabetically), and the total number of valid votes cast across the entire election. For example, given [["Smith", "North", true], ["Jones", "South", false], ["Smith", "South", true]], the output is ["Smith", 2].

title: Bus Route Passengers
spec: Create a function called `simulate(stops, capacity)`. Each stop event is an array with a stop name string, a number of boarding passengers, and a number of departing passengers. The bus starts empty. At each stop, departing passengers leave first, then boarding passengers enter, but only up to the bus capacity. Any boarding passengers who cannot fit are left behind. The function must return an array of two elements: the total number of passengers left behind across all stops, and the highest number of passengers on the bus at any point. For example, given [["Main", 5, 0], ["Oak", 3, 2]] and capacity 5, the output is [1, 5].

title: Traffic Intersection Flow
spec: Write a function called `analyze(counts)`. A congestion period is defined as consecutive minutes where the vehicle count is strictly greater than fifty. A quiet period is consecutive minutes where the count is twenty or less. The function must find the longest congestion period and the longest quiet period. It should return an array containing two elements: a boolean indicating whether the longest congestion period is strictly longer than the longest quiet period, and a number representing the highest single-minute vehicle count recorded. For example, given [10, 15, 60, 70, 55, 12, 10], the output is [true, 70].

title: Manuscript Dialogue Counter
spec: Implement a function called `analyze(manuscript)`. Dialogue is defined as any text enclosed in double quotes. The function must extract all dialogue snippets, ignoring the surrounding text. It should calculate the number of words in each dialogue snippet, treating any continuous sequence of alphabetical letters as a word. The function must return an array containing two numbers: the total number of dialogue snippets found, and the maximum word count among all snippets. For example, given the text 'He said, "Hello there!" and she replied, "Hi!"', the output is [2, 2].

title: Retail Sales Spikes
spec: Create a function called `detect(sales)`. A sales spike is defined as a day where the sales number is strictly greater than the sales on both the preceding and following days. The magnitude of a spike is its sales number minus the average of the sales on the preceding and following days. The first and last days cannot be spikes. The function must return an array of two numbers: the total count of spikes, and the highest magnitude among all spikes rounded to the nearest integer. If there are no spikes, return [0, 0]. For example, given [100, 200, 150, 300, 100], the output is [2, 175].

title: Laboratory Reagent Tracker
spec: Write a function called `track(reagents, margin)`. Each record is an array with three elements: a chemical name string, the current volume in milliliters (a number), and the average daily usage in milliliters (a number). The function should determine how many full days each chemical will last. A chemical is critically low if its days remaining is strictly less than the safety margin. The function must return an array containing two things: a boolean being true if any chemical is critically low, and an array of the names of the critically low chemicals, sorted alphabetically. For example, given [["Acid", 100, 30], ["Base", 500, 10]] and margin 5, the output is [true, ["Acid"]].

title: Volunteer Participation Tracker
spec: Implement a function called `evaluate(logs)`. Each log is an array containing a volunteer name string, a role string, and a number representing hours worked in that session. A volunteer is considered highly active if they have logged at least one session with more than four hours, or if their total hours across all sessions exceed ten. The function must aggregate the logs by volunteer name. It should return an array with two elements: the number of highly active volunteers, and an array of their names sorted alphabetically. For example, given [["Alice", "Guide", 3], ["Bob", "Setup", 5], ["Alice", "Cleanup", 8]], the output is [2, ["Alice", "Bob"]].

title: Memory Block Allocator
spec: Write a function called `allocate(blocks, requests)`. Each process request must be placed in the first memory block that has enough remaining capacity to fit it. When a process is placed, the block's capacity decreases by the request size. If no block can fit a process, the process is skipped. The function must return an array of two numbers: the total number of skipped processes, and the sum of the remaining capacity across all blocks after allocations. For example, given blocks [10, 15] and requests [8, 12, 5], the output is [1, 5].

title: IP Address Subnet Grouping
spec: Create a function called `group(addresses)`. Each valid IP address consists of four numbers separated by dots. The function should extract the first three numbers (the subnet) of each valid IP address. An IP is invalid if it does not have exactly four parts or if any part is not numeric. The function must count occurrences of each subnet. It must return an array containing two elements: a boolean indicating if any subnet appears more than twice, and an array of the unique valid subnets sorted by their frequency in descending order, with alphabetical order for ties. For example, given "192.168.1.10, 192.168.1.20, 10.0.0.1", the output is [false, ["192.168.1", "10.0.0"]].

title: Wind Speed Gust Detector
spec: Implement a function called `detect(records, baseline)`. Each record is an array with a station identifier string, a sustained wind number, and a peak gust number. A station is reporting a dangerous gust if its peak gust exceeds the baseline speed and is also more than fifty percent higher than its sustained wind. The function must return an array containing two elements: the number of stations reporting dangerous gusts, and an array of their station identifiers sorted alphabetically. For example, given [["StationA", 20, 35], ["StationB", 30, 40]] and baseline 30, the output is [1, ["StationA"]].

title: Museum Gallery Visitors
spec: Write a function called `calculate(visitors)`. The museum breaks its day into viewing periods of four hours each. The first four numbers belong to period one, the next four to period two, and so on. If the array length is not a multiple of four, the last period is considered partial. The function should calculate the total visitors for each period. It must return an array of two numbers: the maximum visitor total achieved in any complete four-hour period, and the total visitor count from any partial period. For example, given an array of six numbers all being 10, the output is [40, 20].

title: Board Game Tile Advancement
spec: Create a function called `simulate(cards, length)`. A player starts at tile zero. For each card drawn, if the number is prime, the player moves forward by that amount. If the number is composite, the player moves backward by one tile (but cannot drop below tile zero). The number one is neither prime nor composite, so the player does not move. If the player's position reaches or exceeds the board length, they finish the track. The function must return an array of two elements: a boolean that is true if the player finished the track, and a number representing the total number of cards drawn before finishing or running out of cards. For example, given [4, 5, 6, 7] and length 10, the output is [true, 4].

title: Customer Support Ticket Transfers
spec: Implement a function called `trace(logs)`. Each log is an array containing a ticket identifier string and a department name string representing where the ticket was routed. The function should group the routing history for each ticket. A resolved-on-first-contact ticket is one that was routed to exactly one department. The function must return an array containing two things: the number of tickets resolved on first contact, and an array of the names of the departments that received at least one ticket as its very first routing, with duplicates removed and sorted alphabetically. For example, given [["T1", "Billing"], ["T2", "Tech"], ["T1", "Escalation"]], the output is [1, ["Billing", "Tech"]].

title: Telescope Star Image Stacking
spec: Write a function called `filter(measurements, limit)`. The function first calculates the average of all measurements. Any measurement whose absolute difference from this average is strictly greater than the deviation limit is considered an anomaly. The function should create a new array discarding the anomalies. It must return an array of two numbers: the number of discarded anomalies, and the new average of the remaining clean measurements rounded down to the nearest whole number. For example, given [10, 12, 11, 50, 9] and limit 15, the output is [1, 10].

title: University Course Prerequisites
spec: Create a function called `sequence(attempts)`. Each attempt is an array with three elements: a course code string, a credits number, and a prerequisite course code string (or an empty string if none). A course is successfully enrolled if its prerequisite has already been successfully enrolled earlier in the array, or if it has no prerequisite. The function must aggregate the total credits of all successfully enrolled courses. It should return an array containing two elements: a boolean indicating if any enrollment attempt failed due to a missing prerequisite, and the total credits of successfully enrolled courses. For example, given [["MATH1", 3, ""], ["PHYS2", 4, "PHYS1"], ["MATH2", 3, "MATH1"]], the output is [true, 6].

title: Laboratory Equipment Usage
spec: Implement a function called `summarize(logs)`. Each log is an array containing an equipment name string, a start hour number, and an end hour number (both integers from zero to twenty-four). The function must calculate the total hours each piece of equipment was used, assuming no overlapping logs for the same equipment. It should return an array containing two elements: the name of the equipment with the most total hours (resolving ties alphabetically), and a number representing the total usage hours across all equipment. For example, given [["Microscope", 9, 11], ["Centrifuge", 13, 15], ["Microscope", 14, 15]], the output is ["Microscope", 5].

title: Submarine Depth Ping
spec: Write a function called `survey(echoes)`. Each echo is an array containing a coordinate string, a transmission time number, and a reception time number. The depth at a coordinate is calculated as the difference between reception and transmission times, multiplied by a sound speed of seven hundred and fifty. The function must process all echoes to find the deepest point. It should return an array of two elements: a boolean indicating if any depth exceeded ten thousand, and the coordinate string of the deepest location (ties broken alphabetically). For example, given [["A1", 0, 10], ["B2", 5, 25]], the output is [true, "B2"].

title: Broadband Outage Rebates
spec: Create a function called `evaluate(outages, threshold)`. Each record is an array containing a customer account string, an outage start time number, and an outage end time number. The duration of an outage is the end time minus the start time. A customer is eligible for a rebate if any single outage duration is strictly greater than the threshold. The function must find all eligible customers. It should return an array with two elements: a boolean that is true if there is at least one eligible customer, and an array of the eligible customer accounts sorted alphabetically, without duplicates. For example, given [["C1", 10, 50], ["C2", 100, 110]] and threshold 20, the output is [true, ["C1"]].

title: Software Feature Prioritization
spec: Implement a function called `optimize(proposals, capacity)`. Each proposal is an array with a feature name string, an estimated hours number, and an impact score number. The function should sort the proposals by impact score from highest to lowest. It must then simulate selecting proposals in that order until the remaining capacity cannot accommodate the hours of the next proposal, at which point the selection process stops immediately. The function must return an array of two elements: the number of features successfully selected, and the remaining unused capacity hours. For example, given [["Chat", 30, 10], ["Export", 20, 20], ["Search", 50, 30]] and capacity 60, the output is [1, 10].

title: Power Grid Voltage Drops
spec: Write a function called `monitor(voltages, threshold)`. The grid is considered unstable if there are three consecutive measurements strictly below the minimum threshold. The function must simulate monitoring the grid sequentially and count how many times it becomes unstable. Once instability is detected, the counter increments, the sequence resets, and the next three consecutive low measurements trigger another instability event. The function should return an array containing three elements: a boolean indicating if the grid ever experienced two or more instability events, the total count of instability events, and the lowest voltage measurement recorded overall. For example, given [220, 200, 200, 200, 230, 190, 190, 190, 190] and threshold 210, the output is [true, 2, 190].

title: Wardrobe Costume Penalties
spec: Create a function called `assess(returns, fee)`. Each record is an array containing a character name string, a days kept number, and a fabric condition string (clean, worn, or torn). The basic charge is the days kept multiplied by the daily fee. If the condition is torn, a flat repair penalty of seventy-five is added to the charge for that costume. The function must return an array of two elements: a boolean indicating whether any costume was returned torn, and a number representing the total collected charges including penalties across all costumes. For example, given [["Hero", 3, "clean"], ["Villain", 2, "torn"]] and fee 10, the output is [true, 125].

title: Fishery Catch Quotas
spec: Implement a function called `estimate(reports)`. Each report is an array containing a species name string, a number of nets cast, and an average catch per net number. The total catch for a report is the nets cast multiplied by the average catch. The function must aggregate the total catch for each unique species. It should return an array containing two elements: the species name string that yielded the highest overall catch (ties resolved alphabetically), and the total catch amount across all species. For example, given [["Salmon", 10, 5], ["Tuna", 20, 2], ["Salmon", 5, 5]], the output is ["Salmon", 115].

title: Magazine Print Runs
spec: Write a function called `calculate(batches)`. Each batch is an array containing a region name string, a count of active subscribers as a number, and a count of promotional copies as a number. The total required copies for a region is active subscribers plus promotional copies. The printing press requires the total copies per region to be a multiple of fifty; any partial batch must be rounded up to the next multiple of fifty. The function must return an array of two numbers: the total number of printed copies across all regions, and the total number of surplus copies (printed copies minus required copies). For example, given [["North", 120, 10], ["South", 40, 5]], the output is [200, 25].

title: Astronomy Exoplanet Filter
spec: Write an entry function `evaluate` that filters habitable planets. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains a star name string, a planet name string, a distance number, and a boolean indicating if liquid water is present. Create a helper function to determine the habitability of a single planet based on its distance and water presence. A planet is considered habitable if its distance is between zero point eight and one point five inclusive, and the water boolean is true. Iterate through all systems using the helper. Build and return an array containing only the names of the habitable planets. Include a short driver to demonstrate with a sample array.

title: Podcast Episode Queue
spec: Write an entry function `queue` that calculates total remaining listen time. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array provides an episode title string, a duration in minutes as a number, and a boolean indicating if it has already been played. Create a helper function that calculates the adjusted duration for a single episode. Skip any episodes where the played boolean is true. For the remaining episodes, if the title contains the word sponsor in lowercase, subtract two minutes from its duration. Maintain a running total of the duration. Return the final total as a single number. Include a short driver to demonstrate with sample inputs.

title: Boarding Pass Validator
spec: Write an entry function `validate` that filters valid flight passes. The input is an array of barcode strings. Create a helper function to check if an individual barcode string meets the valid criteria. A barcode is considered valid if it starts with the uppercase letter F, has a length of exactly twelve characters, and ends with a digit greater than zero. Iterate through the array and check each string using the helper. Keep a count of how many barcodes are valid, and store the first valid barcode found. Return an array containing the total count of valid passes as a number, followed by the first valid barcode string. Include a short driver to demonstrate.

title: Wildlife Camera Trap
spec: Write an entry function `countSightings` that aggregates animal observations. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array holds a species name string, an observation count number, and a boolean for night vision mode. Delegate the calculation of an individual observation adjusted count to a helper function. If night vision is true and the species is either raccoon or panther, double the observation count for that entry. Sum the total number of animals observed across all entries. Also, track if any panthers were seen at all using a boolean flag. Return an array where the first element is the total animal count and the second element is the boolean flag for panthers. Include a driver to demonstrate.

title: Drone Battery Estimator
spec: Write an entry function `estimate` that calculates battery drain for a drone. The input is an array of arrays, each representing a flight plan with a distance in meters as a number, a wind speed number, and a boolean for a heavy payload. Use a helper function to compute the battery drain for a single flight plan. The base drain is the distance divided by ten. If the wind speed is greater than fifteen, add twenty to the drain. Finally, if the heavy payload boolean is true, multiply the current drain by one point five. Sum the drain across all missions. Return the total drain rounded down to the nearest integer. Include a short driver.

title: Hydroponic Nutrient Mixer
spec: Write an entry function `mix` that calculates nutrient drops for indoor farming. The input is an array of arrays, where each contains a tank identifier string, a volume in liters as a number, and a boolean indicating if blooming nutrients are needed. Create a helper function to determine the exact number of nutrient drops for one tank. Standard tanks need two drops per liter, while tanks needing blooming nutrients require three drops per liter. Accumulate the total drops across all tanks. Track the identifier of the tank that requires the highest number of drops. Return an array with the total drops number and the highest tank identifier string. Include a driver to demonstrate.

title: Subway Fare Capper
spec: Write an entry function `calculateFares` that computes weekly transit costs. The input is an array of arrays, where each trip has a zone string, a distance number, and a boolean for peak hours. Extract the cost calculation for a single trip into a helper function. The base cost of any trip is two. If the trip occurs during peak hours, add one to the cost. If the zone is exactly the word suburban, add another one. Maintain a running total of the costs. If the accumulated total exceeds thirty five at any point, cap it at thirty five and ignore further costs. Return the final total cost as a single number. Include a short driver.

title: Vinyl Record Appraiser
spec: Write an entry function `appraise` that values a record collection. The input is an array of arrays, each providing a title string, an age in years as a number, and a boolean for mint condition. Use a helper function to determine the financial value of a single record. The base value of every record is ten. Add one to the value for every year of its age. If the mint condition boolean is true, double the total value of that specific record. Maintain a list of titles for records whose final calculated value is strictly greater than fifty. Return an array containing only these high value title strings. Include a driver.

title: Mountain Bike Setup
spec: Write an entry function `tune` that determines suspension pressures. The input is an array of arrays, each containing a rider name string, a weight in pounds as a number, and a boolean for an aggressive riding style. Create a helper function to calculate the precise suspension pressure for an individual rider. To calculate the pressure, multiply the weight by zero point six. If the aggressive boolean is true, add fifteen to that pressure. Keep a count of how many riders require a pressure greater than one hundred fifty. Also, track the highest calculated pressure overall. Return an array containing the high pressure count and the highest pressure number. Include a driver.

title: Barista Tip Distributor
spec: Write an entry function `distribute` that splits a fixed tip pool. The input is an array of arrays, each with a staff name string, hours worked as a number, and a boolean indicating if they are a manager. Managers do not receive tips. Use a helper function to compute the eligible hours for a single staff member, returning zero for managers. Sum the total valid hours worked by all non managers. The total tip pool is exactly two hundred. For each non manager, their share is their hours divided by the total non manager hours, multiplied by the tip pool. Return an array of arrays, where each inner array holds the staff name string and their tip amount number rounded down. Include a driver.

title: Meteor Shower Predictor
spec: Write an entry function `predict` that finds the best meteor viewing spot. The input is an array of arrays, each providing a region name string, an hourly meteor count number, and a boolean indicating if the skies are clear. Create a helper function to evaluate if an individual observation qualifies as a major event. Discard any observations where the clear skies boolean is false. Among the remaining, find the region with the highest hourly count. If that maximum count is greater than fifty, the helper should classify it as a major event. Return an array containing the top region name string, its meteor count number, and the major event boolean flag. Include a driver.

title: Language Flashcard Scheduler
spec: Write an entry function `schedule` that determines review intervals. The input is an array of arrays, each holding a vocabulary word string, a current streak number, and a boolean indicating if the last guess was correct. Use a helper function to process a single flashcard and return its updated streak and next review day. For each card, if the correct boolean is true, add one to the streak; if false, set the streak to zero. Calculate the next review time in days by multiplying the updated streak by two, then adding one. Build and return an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the word string and its next review time number. Include a driver.

title: Board Game Victory Points
spec: Write an entry function `tally` that calculates final scores. The input is an array of arrays, each representing a player with a name string, a gold coin count number, and a boolean indicating if they control the capital city. Delegate the victory point calculation for a single player to a helper function. A player receives one victory point for every three gold coins, rounded down. If they control the capital, add five bonus points to their score. Track the highest score and the name of the player who achieved it. Return an array containing the winning player name string and their final score number. Include a short driver.

title: Electric Vehicle Route Planner
spec: Write an entry function `plan` that filters charging stops. The input is an array of arrays, each providing a city name string, a distance from the start in miles as a number, and a boolean for fast charging capability. Create a helper function to evaluate if the distance and charging capabilities make a station a valid stop. The vehicle can travel a maximum of two hundred miles between stops. Iterate through the stations. Add a station to your selected route only if the distance from the previously selected station exceeds one hundred fifty miles, or if the fast charging boolean is true and the distance is at least one hundred miles. Return an array of the selected city name strings. Include a driver.

title: Scuba Dive Decompression
spec: Write an entry function `dive` that calculates safety penalties. The input is an array of arrays, each containing a diver name string, a maximum depth in meters as a number, and a boolean indicating if nitrox gas was used. Use a helper function to calculate the penalty minutes for a single dive log. The standard safe depth limit is thirty meters. If nitrox was used, the safe limit becomes forty meters. If a diver exceeds their respective limit, calculate penalty minutes by subtracting the limit from their depth and multiplying by two. Build a list of names of divers who accrued any penalty minutes. Return this array of name strings. Include a driver.

title: Wedding Guest Seating
spec: Write an entry function `seat` that calculates table requirements. The input is an array of arrays, each holding a family name string, a guest count number, and a boolean indicating if a high chair is needed. Create a helper function to process a single family response and extract their guest and high chair counts. Sum the total guest count across all responses. Calculate the total line length deployed if all kites are flown to their maximum limit. Return a list containing this total length, followed by a list of shapes that have stabilizing tails. Provide a complete module with this function and a small driver block that passes the example input and logs the output. Example: input [["delta", 150, true], ["diamond", 100, true], ["box", 200, false]] outputs [450, ["delta", "diamond"]].

title: Marching Band Formation Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(formations)` that assesses an array of marching band routines. Each routine has a shape name, an array of coordinate distances, the number of marchers, and a boolean indicating if instruments are raised. Calculate the total distance covered by summing the coordinate distances. Divide the total distance by the number of marchers to find the spread factor. A routine is considered complex if the spread factor is greater than five and the instruments are raised. Find the maximum total distance across all routines. Return an array containing the maximum distance, a boolean true if any routine is complex, and an array of arrays where each inner array contains the shape name, the spread factor, and the complex boolean. Example: a star shape with distances ten, fifteen, and twenty, ten marchers, and raised instruments has a spread of four point five and is not complex.

title: Ski Jump Style Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(jumps)` that takes an array of jump records. Each jump has a skier name, a base distance, an array of five judge scores, and a wind compensation factor. For each jump, discard the highest and lowest judge scores, then sum the remaining three. Calculate the total points by adding the base distance, the valid judge sum, and the wind compensation. Determine if the jump is eligible for a record by checking if the total points exceed two hundred and the distance is at least one hundred thirty. Compile the results into a new summary. Return an array where each element is an array containing the skier name, the calculated total points, a boolean indicating if it is a record, and an array of the three kept judge scores. Example: a jump by eagle with distance one hundred, scores twenty, fifteen, ten, fifteen, ten, and wind five gives eagle, one hundred forty-five, false, and array fifteen, fifteen, ten.

title: Paintball Elimination Tracker
spec: Write a function `tally(matches)` that processes an array of match outcomes. Each outcome contains a team name, the number of opponents eliminated, the number of friendly fire penalties, whether the team captured the flag, and an array of player survival times. Calculate a team score by awarding ten points per elimination, subtracting five points per penalty, and adding fifty points for a flag capture. Compute the average survival time from the player times. A team is considered a top contender if their score is over one hundred and their average survival time is at least ten minutes. Accumulate these statistics across all matches for each team. Return an array of arrays where each inner array contains the team name, total score, the top contender boolean, and an array of all their match average survival times. Example: a team with five eliminations, zero penalties, flag captured, and times twelve and fourteen returns the team name, one hundred, true, and an array containing thirteen.

title: Haunted House Scare Rater
spec: Write a function `rate(rooms)` that assesses an array of room configurations. Each room specifies a theme name, an array of prop scare values, an actor intensity multiplier, and a boolean indicating if the room has strobe lights. For each room, compute the base scare level by summing the prop scare values. Multiply this base level by the actor intensity. If the room has strobe lights, add a flat bonus of twenty to the scare level. Determine if the room is restricted by checking if the final scare level exceeds one hundred. Keep a running tally of the total scare level across all rooms. Create a listing of approved room profiles. Return an array containing the overall total scare level, a boolean true if any room is restricted, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the theme name, final scare score, and restricted boolean. Example: a zombie room with props five and ten, actor multiplier two, and no strobes gives a score of thirty, not restricted.

title: Karaoke Lineup Organizer
spec: Write a function `organize(requests)` that manages an array of song requests. Each request provides a singer name, a song duration in seconds, an array of previous performance scores, and a boolean for whether they require a lyrics screen. Calculate the average of the previous scores. If a singer has an average score above eighty and the song is under two hundred seconds, they are marked as a vip performer. Order the requests so that vip performers go first, preserving their original order, followed by the rest. Calculate the total running time of the lineup. Return an array containing the total running time, a boolean indicating if the lineup is complete, and an array of arrays for the scheduled performances where each inner array contains the singer name, the duration, and the vip boolean. Example: an eight second song by star with average ninety and lyrics required becomes a vip performer placed first.

title: Food Truck Revenue Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(trucks)` that takes an array of daily truck sales. Each truck reports a vendor name, an array of hourly sales figures, a fixed parking fee, and a boolean indicating if they sell dessert. Calculate the gross income for each truck by summing the hourly sales. Deduct the parking fee to find the net profit. If a truck sells dessert and makes a net profit over five hundred, they are flagged as a premium vendor. Track the highest net profit among all trucks. Return an array containing the highest profit as a number, a boolean true if any dessert truck had a loss, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the vendor name, the net profit, and the premium vendor boolean. Example: a dessert truck with sales of two hundred and four hundred, and a fee of one hundred, nets five hundred, so it is premium.

title: Laser Tag Match Summarizer
spec: Write a function `summarize(players)` that processes an array of player statistics. Each player provides an alias string, an array of shot distances, the number of hits scored, and a boolean for whether they used a sniper loadout. Calculate the total shots fired as the length of the shot distances array. Compute the accuracy percentage by dividing hits by total shots and multiplying by one hundred. Determine the maximum shot distance for the player. A player is awarded a marksman badge if their accuracy is above forty percent, their maximum distance is over fifty, and they used a sniper loadout. Find the average accuracy across all players. Return an array with the average accuracy, a boolean true if more than two marksman badges were awarded, and an array of arrays where each inner array contains the alias, the accuracy, and the badge boolean. Example: a sniper with ten hits out of twenty shots and a max distance of sixty earns a badge.

title: Miniature Train Layout Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(segments)` that analyzes an array of track segments. Each segment has a shape name, an array of curve radii, a length value, and a boolean indicating if it includes a switch track. Calculate the total track length by adding up all segment lengths. For each segment, check if it contains any curve radius smaller than fifteen; if so, flag it as a sharp curve. A segment is considered complex if it has a sharp curve and includes a switch track. Count the total number of complex segments. Determine if the layout is suitable for high speed by ensuring no sharp curves exist anywhere. Return an array containing the total length, the high speed boolean, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the shape name, the length, and the complex boolean. Example: a segment named loop with length twenty, radii ten and twenty, and a switch track is complex.

title: Pinball Score Multiplier
spec: Write a function `calculate(bumpers)` that processes an array of bumper interactions. Each interaction includes a bumper type string, a base point value, an array of recent hit timestamps, and a boolean indicating if the bumper is lit. For each interaction, count how many hits occurred in the array. If the bumper is lit, multiply the base points by two. If the number of hits is greater than three, add a combo bonus of fifty points. Compute the total score for the bumper. A bumper triggers a jackpot if its total score exceeds two hundred and it is lit. Accumulate the total score across all interactions. Return an array containing the total accumulated score, a boolean true if any jackpot was triggered, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the bumper type, the calculated score, and the jackpot boolean. Example: a lit pop bumper with base one hundred and four hits scores two hundred fifty and triggers a jackpot.

title: Bungee Jump Rope Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess(jumpers)` that evaluates an array of bungee jumper profiles. Each jumper has a client name, a body weight, an array of previous jump heights, and a boolean indicating if they requested a water dip. Calculate the highest jump from their previous heights. Determine the required rope tension by multiplying the body weight by a safety factor of one point five. If a water dip is requested, reduce the tension by ten percent. A jumper is marked as experienced if their highest jump exceeds fifty meters and they have more than two previous jumps. Sum the total tension required for all jumpers for equipment planning. Return an array containing the total tension, a boolean true if any jumper requested a water dip, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the client name, the calculated tension, and the experienced boolean. Example: an eighty kilo jumper requesting a dip with jumps of twenty and sixty gets a tension of one hundred eight and is experienced.

title: Demolition Derby Damage Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(cars)` that processes an array of car status reports. Each car has a driver name, an initial structural integrity value, an array of impact forces received, and a boolean indicating if the engine is smoking. Calculate the total damage sustained by summing the impact forces. Subtract the total damage from the initial integrity to find the current condition. A car is considered eliminated if its current condition falls below zero or if the engine is smoking. Find the driver with the highest remaining condition among those not eliminated. Return an array containing the winning driver name, the winning condition number, a boolean true if all cars were eliminated, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the driver name, current condition, and eliminated boolean. Example: a car with integrity one hundred, hits of thirty and forty, and no smoke survives with condition thirty.

title: Yo-Yo Trick Combo Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(combos)` that evaluates an array of yo-yo routines. Each routine has a trick name, a base difficulty score, an array of mistake deductions, and a boolean indicating if it ended with a successful bind. Calculate the total deductions by summing the array. Subtract the deductions from the base difficulty to get the net score. A routine is considered flawless if there are no deductions and it ended with a successful bind. If a routine is flawless, multiply the net score by one point two. Keep track of the highest net score achieved across all routines. Return an array containing the highest net score, a boolean true if at least one routine was flawless, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the trick name, the net score, and the flawless boolean. Example: a trick with base fifty, empty deductions, and successful bind scores sixty and is flawless.

title: Origami Project Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(models)` that assesses an array of origami designs. Each design has a model name, a starting paper size, an array of fold complexity ratings, and a boolean indicating if it requires cutting. Calculate the total complexity by summing the ratings in the array. Determine the estimated time in minutes by multiplying the total complexity by two. If cutting is required, add fifteen minutes to the estimated time and flag the model as non-traditional. Find the average estimated time across all designs. Return an array containing the average time, a boolean true if any model is non-traditional, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the model name, the estimated time, and the non-traditional boolean. Example: a crane with paper size twenty, fold ratings of two, three, and one, and no cutting takes twelve minutes and is traditional.

title: Dog Agility Run Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(runs)` that evaluates an array of dog agility performances. Each run contains a dog name, a standard course time, an array of obstacle completion times, and a boolean indicating if a hurdle was knocked down. Calculate the actual course time by summing the obstacle times. If a hurdle was knocked down, add a five-second penalty to the actual time. Determine the time difference by subtracting the standard course time from the actual time. A dog earns a qualifying certificate if their time difference is less than or equal to zero and no hurdle was knocked down. Accumulate the total number of qualifying certificates. Return an array containing the total certificates, a boolean true if any dog finished under the standard time regardless of penalties, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the dog name, the final actual time, and the certificate boolean. Example: a dog with times of five and ten, standard time twenty, and no knocked hurdles finishes in fifteen and qualifies.

title: Pogo Stick Endurance Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(sessions)` that processes an array of pogo stick workouts. Each session has an athlete name, an expected jump goal, an array of continuous jump counts, and a boolean indicating if a trick was performed. Sum the jump counts to find the total jumps for the session. Find the maximum continuous jumps from the array. A session is deemed a success if the total jumps exceed the expected goal and a trick was performed. If the maximum continuous jumps exceed one hundred, the athlete earns an iron legs badge. Compute the total jumps across all sessions. Return an array containing the total overall jumps, a boolean true if any iron legs badge was earned, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the athlete name, total jumps, and the success boolean. Example: an athlete with a goal of fifty, jumps of twenty and forty, and a trick performed has sixty total jumps and a successful session.

title: Trampoline Park Safety Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(zones)` that analyzes an array of trampoline zone reports. Each zone contains a zone name, a maximum weight limit, an array of current jumper weights, and a boolean indicating if a staff member is present. Calculate the total current weight by summing the jumper weights. Calculate the utilization percentage by dividing the current weight by the maximum limit.
