A zone is marked as hazardous if the utilization exceeds eighty percent and no staff member is present. If the utilization is under fifty percent, the zone is marked as underutilized. Count the number of hazardous zones. Return an array containing the total number of hazardous zones, a boolean true if all zones have staff present, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the zone name, the utilization percentage, and the hazardous boolean. Example: a zone with limit five hundred, jumper weights of two hundred and two hundred fifty, and no staff is ninety percent utilized and hazardous.

title: Hang Glider Flight Profiler
spec: Write a function `profile(flights)` that evaluates an array of hang glider trips. Each trip includes a pilot name, a starting altitude, an array of thermal lift amounts, and a boolean indicating if strong headwinds were encountered. Calculate the total lift gained by summing the thermal amounts. Add the total lift to the starting altitude, then subtract fifty if strong headwinds were encountered, to determine the final altitude. A flight is classified as an endurance flight if the total lift gained exceeds five hundred and no strong headwinds were present. Find the maximum final altitude across all trips. Return an array containing the maximum final altitude, a boolean true if any flight was an endurance flight, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the pilot name, final altitude, and endurance boolean. Example: a pilot starting at one thousand, lifts of three hundred and three hundred, and no headwinds reaches sixteen hundred and achieves endurance.

title: Roller Derby Jam Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(jams)` that processes an array of roller derby jam records. Each jam contains a jammer name, the number of opposing blockers on the track, an array of points scored per pass, and a boolean indicating if the jammer was sent to the penalty box. Calculate the total points for the jam by summing the array. If the jammer went to the penalty box, subtract five points from the total. A jam is designated a power jam if the total points exceed twenty and the jammer never went to the penalty box. Determine the average points scored per pass. Keep a running total of points scored across all jams. Return an array containing the overall points, a boolean true if any power jam occurred, and an array of arrays where each inner array holds the jammer name, total points, and the power jam boolean. Example: a jammer with three passes scoring ten, eight, and four points, and no penalty box visits scores twenty-two and earns a power jam.

title: Cargo Ship Container Stacking
spec: Write a function `stack(containers)` that arranges shipping containers into holds based on destination and weight. The input is a list of objects where each has a destination port, a weight in tons, and a flag indicating if it requires refrigeration. You must distribute these into a list of holds, each with a maximum weight capacity of five hundred tons. Refrigerated containers must go into the first hold, which has cooling capabilities, unless it is full. Return a list containing the number of successfully loaded containers, a boolean indicating if any refrigerated containers had to be placed in a non-cooling hold because the first was full, and a list of lists containing the destination ports for each hold. Example: given one refrigerated container for port alpha weighing two hundred tons and one normal container for port beta weighing four hundred tons, return a list containing two, false, and a list of two lists where the first has port alpha and the second has port beta.

title: Zoo Enclosure Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(animals)` that assigns newly arrived animals to specific zoo zones. The input is a list of animal records containing a species name, an aggression level from one to ten, and a boolean indicating if it is aquatic. You must group the animals into a sequence of enclosures such that no enclosure has more than three animals. Furthermore, an animal with an aggression level above seven must be placed in an enclosure by itself. Aquatic animals must be placed in enclosures designated for water, which we represent by appending the word water to the first animal species placed in that enclosure. Return a list containing the total number of enclosures used, a boolean indicating if any aggressive animals required solitary confinement, and the list of hyphen-separated species strings for each enclosure. Example: given a highly aggressive tiger and a peaceful turtle that is aquatic, return a list containing two, true, and a list containing the string tiger and the string turtle water.

title: Cave Exploration Mapper
spec: Create a function `map(segments)` that processes underground cave paths. The input is a sequence of path observations, each having a cardinal direction, a length in meters, and a boolean noting if the passage is flooded. You must track the total length of valid passages and the sequence of directions taken to find the deepest point. If a segment is flooded and its length is over fifty meters, it is considered impassable, and you must ignore all subsequent segments. Return a list containing the total valid distance traveled as a number, a boolean representing whether the explorers had to turn back due to an impassable flood, and a list of the cardinal directions traveled up to the stopping point. Example: given north ten meters not flooded, and east sixty meters flooded, return a list with seventy, true, and a list with north and east.

title: Microscope Slide Cataloger
spec: Implement a function `catalog(slides)` that organizes laboratory slide preparations. The input is a list of slide objects detailing a specimen name, a magnification integer, and a flag showing if the sample is stained. Group the specimens by magnification level into separate arrays. Only keep specimens where the magnification is at least one hundred. If a sample is stained, append the word stained to the specimen name. Finally, return a list of summaries where each summary is a list starting with the magnification level, followed by a boolean that is true if all samples at this level are stained, and then the modified specimen names. Example: given an unstained cell at fifty magnification, and a stained tissue at two hundred magnification, return a list containing one inner list that holds two hundred, true, and tissue stained.

title: Wine Tasting Scoring
spec: Provide a function `score(wines)` that evaluates a series of blind wine tasting results. The input is a list of dictionaries with a vineyard name, a numerical score out of one hundred, and a flag indicating if it is a red wine. You need to calculate the average score for red wines and white wines separately. Keep a list of all vineyard names that scored above ninety, prepending the word premium to their names. Return a list containing three elements: the average score of all red wines, a boolean indicating if the red wine average is strictly greater than the white wine average, and a list of the premium vineyard names. Example: given a red wine from estate alpha scoring ninety five and a white wine from estate beta scoring eighty, return ninety five, true, and a list with premium estate alpha.

title: Geocaching Route Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize(caches)` that selects the best hidden containers to visit on a hike. The input list contains records with a location name, a difficulty rating from one to five, and a boolean indicating if a multi-step puzzle is required. You must build a route that collects location names in the order they are visited. Skip any cache with a difficulty of five if a multi-step puzzle is involved, as it takes too long. Accumulate the total difficulty of the visited caches. Stop adding caches to the route once the total difficulty exceeds twenty. Return a list with the total difficulty, a boolean denoting if any multi-step puzzles were included, and a list of the chosen location names. Example: given a forest cache with difficulty three and no puzzle, and a river cache with difficulty five and a puzzle, return three, false, and a list containing just the forest cache.

title: Magic Trick Deck Stacker
spec: Implement a function `prepare(cards)` that arranges a deck of playing cards for an illusion. The input is a list of card objects, each with a suit name, a face value integer, and a boolean indicating if the card is a designated key card. You must separate the deck into two piles: one containing all the key cards and another for the rest. For the non key cards, discard any card with an even face value. Keep a running tally of the sum of the odd face values. Return a list where the first item is the total odd value, the second is a boolean showing if the key card pile has more cards than the odd pile, and the third is a list of the suit names of the key cards in order. Example: given a key card of hearts value five, and a non key of spades value three, return three, false, and a list containing hearts.

title: Cosmetics Ingredient Blender
spec: Create a function `blend(ingredients)` that formulates a lotion mixture from raw components. The input provides a list of components, each detailing an ingredient name, a volume in milliliters, and a flag showing if it is an active chemical. You must combine the ingredients by summing their volumes. If the total volume exceeds one thousand milliliters, you must scale down all individual volumes proportionally so the total equals exactly one thousand. Extract the names of all active chemicals into a separate list. Return a list containing the final total volume, a boolean indicating if any scaling was performed, and the list of active ingredient names. Example: given water at eight hundred milliliters inactive, and serum at four hundred milliliters active, return one thousand, true, and a list with serum.

title: Parachute Rigging Inspector
spec: Write a function `inspect(parachutes)` that validates the safety of skydiving equipment. Each parachute record in the input list has a manufacturer name, a usage count, and a flag indicating if the reserve chute has been repacked within six months. Any parachute with a usage count over two hundred or an outdated reserve repack must be marked as unsafe. Calculate the ratio of safe parachutes to the total number of parachutes. Collect the manufacturer names of the unsafe parachutes into an array. Return a list containing the safety ratio as a decimal, a boolean indicating if all parachutes are safe, and the list of unsafe manufacturer names. Example: given a safe chute from delta and an unsafe chute from echo, return zero point five, false, and a list with echo.

title: Kayak Rapid Navigator
spec: Implement a function `navigate(rapids)` that plans a river descent. The input is a list of river sections, each with a section name, a class rating from one to six, and a boolean denoting if there is a mandatory portage. You must traverse the sections, adding the section names to a path list. If you encounter a class six rapid or a mandatory portage, you must record that the river cannot be run continuously and stop adding to the path. Sum the class ratings of the rapids successfully navigated. Return a list consisting of the sum of the navigated ratings, a boolean indicating if the entire river was run continuously, and the list of successfully navigated section names. Example: given calm water class one without portage and waterfall class six with portage, return one, false, and a list with calm water.

title: Treasure Hunt Clue Sequence
spec: Create a function `verify(clues)` that checks the order of hints in a scavenger hunt. The input list contains clues with a hint phrase, an expected step number, and a boolean flag determining if the clue involves digging. You must sort the clues by their expected step number. Keep track of the total number of digging locations. If any two consecutive clues have the same expected step number, the sequence is invalid. Extract the hint phrases into an ordered list. Return a list containing the total number of digging clues, a boolean representing if the sequence is perfectly valid with no duplicate steps, and the ordered list of hint phrases. Example: given a dig clue at step two and a look clue at step one, return one, true, and a list with the look clue phrase followed by the dig clue phrase.

title: Cheese Aging Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(batches)` that checks the maturity of dairy wheels in a cellar. Each batch object in the input has a cheese type, an aging duration in days, and a boolean indicating if a natural rind has formed. A batch is ready for sale if its aging duration is at least ninety days and the rind has formed. Separate the batches into a ready list and an aging list, storing only their cheese types. Calculate the average aging duration of the batches that are not yet ready. Return a list with the average remaining aging duration, a boolean showing if there are more ready batches than aging ones, and the list of ready cheese types. Example: given a ready gouda at one hundred days and an unready brie at ten days, return ten, false, and a list with gouda.

title: Fireworks Show Sequencer
spec: Develop a function `choreograph(shells)` that times the launch of pyrotechnics. The input is a list of fireworks, each having a color name, a fuse delay in seconds, and a flag indicating if it is a grand finale shell. You must calculate the cumulative launch time by adding the fuse delays in order. Group the color names into an array. If a grand finale shell appears, it must be launched simultaneously with the immediately preceding shell, meaning its fuse delay does not add to the total time. Return a list containing the total duration of the show, a boolean that is true if at least one finale shell was included, and the list of colors in order. Example: given a red shell with five seconds delay and a finale blue shell with zero delay, return five, true, and a list with red and blue.

title: Dim Sum Cart Distributor
spec: Write a function `distribute(requests)` that routes food orders to diners. The input list consists of table requests, each containing a dish name, a quantity, and a boolean indicating if the table requires vegetarian food. You must allocate the dishes by compiling a list of dish names for vegetarian tables and a separate list for others. Calculate the total quantity of all dishes ordered. If a vegetarian table requests a dish that has the word meat in its name, disregard that specific request entirely. Return a list containing the total valid quantity of dishes, a boolean indicating if any invalid meat requests were blocked, and the list of vegetarian dish names. Example: given one vegetarian request for bun and one for meat dumpling, return one, true, and a list with bun.

title: Bouldering Wall Route Setter
spec: Implement a function `assess(holds)` that reviews the layout of an indoor climbing wall. The input list provides hold properties, each with a color string, a physical distance from the start in centimeters, and a boolean noting if the hold is a jug which is easy to grip. You must identify all the easy grips and store their colors in a sequence. Calculate the maximum distance between any two consecutive easy grips. If this maximum distance exceeds one hundred centimeters, the route is considered too advanced. Return a list containing the maximum distance found, a boolean indicating if the route is accessible for beginners, and the list of easy grip colors. Example: given a green jug at zero, a red tiny hold at fifty, and a blue jug at one hundred twenty, return one hundred twenty, false, and a list with green and blue.

title: Hot Air Balloon Weight Manager
spec: Create a function `manage(passengers)` that determines if a flight can safely take off. The input list has passenger details including a first name, a weight in kilograms, and a boolean showing if they brought heavy camera gear. Sum the weights of all passengers. Every passenger with heavy camera gear adds an additional fifteen kilograms to their effective weight. If the total effective weight goes over four hundred kilograms, the flight cannot proceed. Keep a list of the first names of passengers carrying camera gear. Return a list with the total effective weight, a boolean that is true if the flight is safe to launch, and the list of photographer names. Example: given one passenger named john weighing eighty with gear, return ninety five, true, and a list with john.

title: Knitting Pattern Stitcher
spec: Write a function `stitch(rows)` that translates a clothing pattern into instructions. The input is a list of row instructions, each specifying a stitch type, a loop count, and a flag indicating if the row uses a contrasting yarn color. You must calculate the total number of loops across all rows. Collect the stitch types of any rows that use the contrasting color into a separate array. If the total loop count exceeds five thousand, the project is considered a large garment. Return a list containing the total loop count, a boolean representing if the project is large, and the array of contrasting stitch types. Example: given fifty loops of purl in regular color and twenty loops of knit in contrast color, return seventy, false, and a list with knit.

title: Blacksmith Forging Temperature Monitor
spec: Provide a function `track(strikes)` that observes the heating and shaping of metal. The input list contains strike records, each with a tool name, a metal temperature in degrees, and a boolean showing if the metal sparked. You must compute the average temperature across all strikes. If the temperature drops below eight hundred degrees, a reheating phase was needed. Compile a list of tool names used during strikes that produced sparks. Return a list containing the average temperature as a number, a boolean indicating if reheating was ever required, and the list of tool names that caused sparks. Example: given a hammer strike at nine hundred sparking, and a mallet strike at seven hundred not sparking, return eight hundred, true, and a list with hammer.

title: Ant Colony Farm Simulator
spec: Implement a function `simulate(ants)` that categorizes the insects in a formicarium. The input is a list of ant records, each with a role name, a forage distance in centimeters, and a boolean denoting if the ant is carrying food. You must sum the forage distances of all ants carrying food to measure gathering efficiency. Collect the role names of the ants that are not carrying food into a scouting array. If more than half the ants are carrying food, the colony is considered well fed. Return a list containing the total forage distance of successful gatherers, a boolean that is true if the colony is well fed, and the list of scouting ant roles. Example: given a worker carrying food ten centimeters, and a soldier without food twenty centimeters, return ten, false, and a list with soldier.

title: Lighthouse Beacon Timing
spec: Create a function `validate(flashes)` that verifies the maritime signaling of a coastal tower. The input is a sequence of flash events, each providing a color string, a duration in seconds, and a boolean showing if an accompanying fog horn sounded. You must calculate the total duration of all flashes. Extract the color strings of any flashes that occurred without a fog horn into an array. A sequence is valid only if the total flash duration is exactly thirty seconds. Return a list with the total flash duration, a boolean indicating if the sequence is valid, and the list of colors that flashed silently. Example: given a white flash for ten seconds with horn, and a red flash for twenty seconds without horn, return thirty, true, and a list with red.

title: Sandcastle Structural Integrity
spec: Write a function `evaluate(towers)` that assesses a beach sculpture. The input list gives tower details, each with a shape name, a height in inches, and a boolean indicating if wet sand was used. Calculate the average height of towers built with wet sand. Any tower built with dry sand that is over ten inches tall is unstable. Keep a list of the shape names of all unstable towers. Return a list containing the average wet sand height, a boolean showing if any unstable towers were found, and the list of unstable shape names. Example: given a cylinder of twelve inches dry sand, and a cone of eight inches wet sand, return eight, true, and a list with cylinder.

title: Jigsaw Puzzle Border Finder
spec: Implement a function `separate(pieces)` that distinguishes edge pieces from the center. The input is a list of puzzle pieces, each having an image feature description, an edge count representing straight sides, and a boolean noting if the piece is a corner piece. You must group the image features of pieces that have at least one straight side into an edge list. Sum the edge counts across all pieces to find the total straight perimeter. If the puzzle has exactly four corner pieces, it is considered complete. Return a list containing the total straight edge count, a boolean denoting if the corner count is exactly four, and the edge list of image features. Example: given a corner with sky and two edges, and a middle piece with grass and zero edges, return two, false, and a list with sky.

title: Synchronized Swimming Routine Planner
spec: Create a function `plan(formations)` that designs an aquatic performance. The input list provides formation configurations, each detailing a shape name, a hold duration in seconds, and a boolean indicating if the swimmers submerge completely. Sum the hold durations to get the total routine length. Collect the shape names of formations where swimmers remain above water. If the total routine length exceeds one hundred twenty seconds and includes at least one submerged formation, it meets competition standards. Return a list with the total routine length, a boolean indicating if competition standards are met, and the list of above water shape names. Example: given a star shape above water for sixty seconds, and a circle submerged for seventy seconds, return one hundred thirty, true, and a list with star.

title: Magic Potion Ingredient Interactions
spec: Write a function `brew(vials)` that calculates the potency of an alchemical mixture. The input is a list of vial contents, each with a substance name, a magical strength integer, and a boolean showing if it is volatile. You must compute the total magical strength by adding the integers. If a volatile substance is added immediately after another volatile substance, its strength is subtracted instead of added. Gather the substance names of all non volatile ingredients into an array. Return a list containing the final magical strength, a boolean indicating if any subtraction occurred due to consecutive volatile ingredients, and the list of stable substance names. Example: given a stable herb strength ten, a volatile root strength five, and another volatile dust strength four, return eleven, true, and a list with herb.

title: Glazier Window Pane Cutter
spec: Provide a function `calculate(panes)` that evaluates glass requirements for a building. The input list contains window specifications, each having a room name, a square footage, and a boolean indicating if frosted glass is required. Sum the square footage of all windows that require frosted glass. Collect the room names for windows that use regular clear glass into a list. If the total area of frosted glass needed exceeds fifty square feet, a bulk discount applies. Return a list with the total frosted square footage, a boolean showing if the bulk discount applies, and the list of room names using clear glass. Example: given a bathroom thirty square feet frosted, and a kitchen forty square feet clear, return thirty, false, and a list with kitchen.

title: Curling Stone Placement Evaluator
spec:
Write a function `evaluate(throws, target)` that determines the scoring for an end of curling. The first parameter is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains a player name, their stone's distance from the center in meters, and their team color. The second parameter is the maximum distance allowed to be in the scoring house. Filter out any throws that are greater than the target distance. Sort the remaining valid stones by distance in ascending order. Determine which team owns the closest stone. Count how many stones that winning team has that are closer than the opponent's closest stone. Return an array containing the winning team color and the integer points scored.
Example: evaluate([["Alice", 2.5, "red"], ["Bob", 1.2, "yellow"], ["Charlie", 3.0, "red"]], 4.0) -> ["yellow", 1]

title: Speed Cubing Turn Counter
spec:
Create a function `analyze(solves)` that processes rubik's cube solve times. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array holds a string of space-separated moves and the time taken in seconds. Parse the string of moves to count the total moves made. Calculate the turns per second for each solve by dividing the move count by the time. Identify if the solve had any time penalties, which occurs if the time ends exactly in point nine nine. Ignore penalized solves when calculating averages. Return an array containing the average turns per second of all valid solves, the best turns per second among valid solves, and a boolean indicating if any solve had a penalty.
Example: analyze([["U R U R", 2.0], ["R U R", 1.99]]) -> [2.0, 2.0, true]

title: Woodpecker Pecking Pattern
spec:
Implement a function `analyze(pecks, threshold)` to evaluate bird activity. The first parameter is an array of arrays containing the bird name, pecks per second, and tree type. The second parameter is the minimum speed threshold. Filter the data to find only those pecking sessions that are faster than or equal to the threshold. Group these valid sessions by bird name and calculate their average pecking speed. Check if each bird ever pecked on an oak tree. Return an array of arrays, each containing the bird name, their average valid speed, and a boolean indicating if they struck an oak tree.
Example: analyze([["Woody", 15, "oak"], ["Chilly", 10, "pine"], ["Woody", 17, "birch"]], 12) -> [["Woody", 16, true]]

title: Woodworking Joint Calculator
spec:
Develop a function `calculate(boards, kerf)` to finalize lumber cut lengths. The boards parameter is an array of arrays detailing board name, initial length in millimeters, and joint type which can be dovetail, mortise, or butt. The kerf parameter is a number representing the saw blade thickness. Adjust the initial board length based on the joint type by adding ten for dovetail, fifteen for mortise, and zero for butt. Subtract the kerf thickness from the adjusted length to determine the final cut size. Check if the final size is below a minimum safety threshold of fifty millimeters. Return an array of arrays containing the board name, the final cut length, and a boolean indicating if the piece is too short to safely cut.
Example: calculate([["side", 100, "dovetail"], ["front", 40, "butt"]], 2) -> [["side", 108, false], ["front", 38, true]]

title: Seagull Chip Stealing Simulation
spec:
Create a function `simulate(flock, chips)` to model beach bird behavior. The flock parameter is an array of arrays representing seagull name, swoop speed, and accuracy percentage. The chips parameter is the total available food pieces. Sort the flock by swoop speed in descending order. Each bird sequentially attempts to steal a chip. The steal succeeds if their accuracy is greater than fifty. Each successful steal reduces the available chips by one. Continue cycling through the flock until no chips remain. Track how many chips each bird successfully stole. Return an array of arrays containing the seagull name, chips stolen, and a boolean if they managed to eat more than five chips.
Example: simulate([["Steven", 60, 80], ["Jonathan", 70, 40]], 1) -> [["Steven", 1, false], ["Jonathan", 0, false]]

title: Ice Sculpting Melt Rate
spec:
Write a function `predict(sculptures, temperature)` to evaluate exhibit lifespans. The sculptures parameter is an array of arrays detailing sculpture name, initial volume in liters, and surface area in square meters. The temperature parameter is the ambient air temperature. Calculate the hourly melt rate by multiplying the surface area by the temperature and dividing by ten. Determine the hours until the volume reaches zero. Check if the melting time is less than twenty four hours. Return an array of arrays containing the sculpture name, the hours until completely melted, and a boolean indicating if it requires an emergency cooling tent.
Example: predict([["swan", 1000, 50], ["castle", 5000, 100]], 10) -> [["swan", 20, true], ["castle", 50, false]]

title: Parkour Course Planner
spec:
Implement a function `plan(obstacles, stamina)` to simulate a free-running route. The obstacles array contains inner arrays with obstacle name, vertical height, and horizontal gap distance. The stamina parameter is the athlete's starting energy. Calculate the energy required for each obstacle by adding the height and gap distance, then multiplying the sum by two. Deduct this energy from the current stamina sequentially for each obstacle. If stamina drops below zero, the run fails at that obstacle. Track the highest obstacle height successfully cleared. Return an array containing the total count of obstacles cleared, the highest cleared height, and a boolean if the entire course was completed.
Example: plan([["wall", 5, 0], ["gap", 0, 4]], 15) -> [1, 5, false]

title: Glacier Movement Tracker
spec:
Create a function `track(glaciers, years)` to project ice sheet changes. The glaciers parameter is an array of arrays providing glacier name, current thickness in meters, and annual retreat rate in meters per year. The years parameter is the duration to simulate. Calculate the final thickness for each glacier by subtracting the retreat rate multiplied by years from the current thickness. If the calculated thickness drops below zero, cap it at exactly zero. Identify if any glacier lost more than half of its original mass. Return an array of arrays containing the glacier name, the final thickness, and a boolean if it melted completely away.
Example: track([["Perito", 100, 2], ["Muir", 50, 6]], 10) -> [["Perito", 80, false], ["Muir", 0, true]]

title: Sumo Wrestling Banzuke
spec:
Write a function `rank(wrestlers, matches)` to update tournament standings. The wrestlers parameter is an array of arrays with wrestler name, current numerical rank, and total wins. The matches parameter is the total number of bouts in the tournament. Determine if a wrestler achieved a winning record, meaning their wins are strictly greater than half of the total matches. If they have a winning record, promote them by subtracting one from their rank. If they have a losing record, demote them by adding one to their rank. Ensure a rank never drops below one. Return an array of arrays containing the wrestler name, their new rank, and a boolean if they achieved a winning record.
Example: rank([["Hakuho", 2, 8], ["Kakuryu", 5, 6]], 15) -> [["Hakuho", 1, true], ["Kakuryu", 6, false]]

title: Harmonica Tablature Converter
spec:
Implement a function `convert(notes, offset)` to translate breath patterns to pitches. The notes parameter is an array of arrays detailing hole number and a direction string of either blow or draw. The offset is a numeric pitch adjustment. Convert the hole and direction into a pitch number by multiplying the hole by two and adding sixty plus the offset. If the direction is draw, add one more to the pitch. Check if the sequence requires any advanced bends by seeing if any note uses hole two with a draw direction. Track the highest pitch played. Return an array containing an array of computed pitches, the highest pitch, and a boolean if bends were required.
Example: convert([[2, "blow"], [2, "draw"]], 0) -> [[64, 65], 65, true]

title: Brass Band Instrument Tuning
spec:
Develop a function `tune(instruments, standard)` to calculate tuning slide adjustments. The instruments parameter is an array of arrays with instrument name, current pitch frequency, and current slide position. The standard parameter is the target pitch frequency. Calculate the pitch deviation from the standard. If the pitch is higher than the standard, the action is to pull the slide. If it is lower, the action is to push the slide. Calculate the adjustment amount in millimeters by taking the absolute deviation and multiplying by three. Return an array of arrays containing the instrument name, the required action string, the adjustment amount, and a boolean indicating if it was already perfectly in tune.
Example: tune([["trumpet", 442, 10], ["trombone", 438, 20]], 440) -> [["trumpet", "pull", 6, false], ["trombone", "push", 6, false]]

title: Double Dutch Tournament
spec:
Create a function `score(teams, duration)` to evaluate jump rope routines. The teams parameter is an array of arrays containing team name, total jumps completed, and number of mistakes. The duration parameter is the length of the routine in minutes. Calculate the final score by multiplying jumps by two and subtracting mistakes multiplied by five. Determine the jump rate per minute. Identify teams that made exactly zero mistakes. Find the team with the highest final score. Return an array containing the winning team name, their score, and a boolean if they delivered a flawless routine with zero mistakes.
Example: score([["Jumpers", 100, 2], ["Skippers", 80, 5]], 2) -> ["Jumpers", 190, false]

title: Pole Vault Height Progression
spec:
Write a function `progress(attempts, target)` to summarize track and field clearances. The attempts parameter is an array of arrays detailing athlete name, attempted height, and a boolean clearance result. The target parameter is the height needed to qualify for the finals. Group the attempts by athlete. For each athlete, find the maximum height where their clearance result was true. Count how many total attempts they made across all heights. Check if their maximum cleared height meets or exceeds the target. Sort the results by highest cleared height in descending order. Return an array of arrays containing athlete name, best cleared height, total attempts, and a boolean if they qualified.
Example: progress([["Bob", 4.5, true], ["Bob", 5.0, false], ["Sue", 4.5, true], ["Sue", 5.0, true]], 5.0) -> [["Sue", 5.0, 2, true], ["Bob", 4.5, 2, false]]

title: High Dive Entry Rater
spec:
Implement a function `rate(dives, difficulty)` to judge water acrobatics. The dives parameter is an array of arrays containing diver name, splash height in meters, and entry angle in degrees. The difficulty parameter is a numeric multiplier. Calculate the base score out of ten by subtracting the splash height and the absolute deviation of the entry angle from ninety degrees. Multiply this base score by the difficulty factor. Discard any final scores that fall below zero by setting them to zero. Identify the dive that achieved the highest final score. Return an array containing the best diver name, their score, and a boolean if their score was perfectly equal to ten times the difficulty.
Example: rate([["Tom", 1.5, 85], ["Jerry", 0.5, 88]], 2.5) -> ["Jerry", 18.75, false]

title: Sand Animation Sequence
spec:
Develop a function `sequence(frames, rate)` to evaluate a live art performance. The frames parameter is an array of arrays providing scene name, sand thickness layer count, and drawing complexity scale. The rate parameter is the desired frames per second. Calculate the time needed in seconds to draw each frame by multiplying thickness by complexity and dividing by ten. Sum these drawing times to find the total sequence duration. Find the name of the scene that takes the longest individual time to draw. Check if the total duration strictly exceeds sixty seconds. Return an array containing the total duration, the longest scene name, and a boolean if the sequence runs over the time limit.
Example: sequence([["desert", 5, 4], ["camel", 3, 8]], 24) -> [4.4, "camel", false]

title: Boomerang Flight Return
spec:
Create a function `simulate(throws, wind)` to model returning trajectories. The throws parameter is an array of arrays detailing thrower name, throwing force, and release angle. The wind parameter is the current wind speed. Calculate the return distance gap by taking the throwing force, subtracting the wind speed, and adding the absolute difference between the release angle and forty five degrees. If this return distance gap is strictly less than five, it is considered a successful catch. Track the outcomes for all competitors. Return an array of arrays containing the thrower name, the calculated return distance gap, and a boolean indicating if the boomerang was caught.
Example: simulate([["Alice", 10, 45], ["Bob", 20, 50]], 7) -> [["Alice", 3, true], ["Bob", 18, false]]

title: Tap Dance Rhythm Analyzer
spec:
Write a function `analyze(taps, tempo)` to group footwork sequences. The taps parameter is an array of arrays with tap type and absolute timing in seconds. The tempo parameter is the song beats per minute. Calculate the expected time between beats by dividing sixty by the tempo. Group the taps into distinct sequences, starting a new sequence whenever the time gap between consecutive taps is strictly greater than one second. Count the total number of grouped sequences. Check if any tap lands perfectly on a beat, meaning its timing modulo the expected beat time is exactly zero. Return an array containing the total sequences, total number of taps, and a boolean if any perfect beats occurred.
Example: analyze([["heel", 0.5], ["toe", 1.0], ["stamp", 3.0]], 120) -> [2, 3, true]

title: Kendo Tournament Matches
spec:
Implement a function `score(strikes, duration)` to officiate a martial arts bout. The strikes parameter is an array of arrays detailing fighter name, target hit string, and time of impact in seconds. The duration parameter is the maximum allowed match time. Assign points based on the target hit where strikes to men or do earn two points, and strikes to kote or tsuki earn one point. Sum the points for each fighter, completely ignoring any strikes that occurred after the maximum match time. The first fighter to reach four points wins instantly. Return an array containing the winning fighter name, their final points, and a boolean indicating if the match ended early before the time limit.
Example: score([["Ken", "men", 10], ["Ryu", "kote", 20], ["Ken", "do", 30]], 180) -> ["Ken", 4, true]

title: Truffle Hunting Yield Evaluator
spec: Write a function evaluate(hunts) to process a list of foraging outings. Each outing includes the duration in hours, the animal type used, and a list of findings with the weight and truffle type. Calculate the total weight of white and black truffles found across all outings. White truffles are valued higher per gram than black ones. If the animal is a pig, it will consume a portion of the finding unless a specific handler flag is set to true, reducing the final weight. Keep a true or false flag for whether the outing was profitable after subtracting fixed animal feed costs. Return a report containing the final total payout, the accumulated weight of each type, and an array of the profitable outing indices.

title: Typewriter Ribbon Wear Simulator
spec: Create a function simulate(documents) that processes an array of text paragraphs to calculate typewriter ink usage. Track the ribbon position and a true or false flag indicating the current spool winding direction. Count the characters typed, noting that spaces do not use ink and capital letters use twice the standard ink impact. When the cumulative impact reaches the ribbon length limit, the spool direction flag must reverse. Calculate the total ink depletion percentage. Output an array of remaining ink levels after each document, the total number of direction reversals, and a boolean indicating if the ribbon needs replacing.

title: Neon Sign Fabrication Estimator
spec: Implement a function fabricate(designs) to calculate materials for custom neon signs. Each design specifies the tube length in inches, the gas type, and the number of sharp bends. Calculate the volume of gas needed, noting that neon and argon require different pressure multipliers. Longer tubes and frequent bends require higher voltage transformers to maintain luminosity. Determine the total length of glass tubing stock required by adding a fixed waste margin per bend. Return the total required voltage, an array of gas volumes needed per design, and a true or false value if any design exceeds standard shop transformer limits.

title: Sled Dog Team Dispatcher
spec: Write a function dispatch(teams) to evaluate the success rate of sled dog configurations. Each team provides a list of dogs with their individual strength, endurance rating, and a true or false leadership capability. A team must have at least one dog with leadership capability in the front position. Calculate the total pulling force by summing the strengths, but apply a fatigue reduction based on the expected trail distance and the average endurance rating of the dogs. Evaluate if the final force is sufficient to pull the sled weight. Return an array of successful team indices, the fastest expected completion time, and a boolean indicating if all teams passed.

title: Maple Syrup Evaporation Tracker
spec: Create a function boil(batches) to simulate turning tree sap into maple syrup. Each batch has an initial sap volume in gallons and a starting sugar percentage. The target is a standard high sugar percentage for syrup. Calculate the volume of water that must be evaporated for each batch. Determine the cords of wood fuel required based on the heat needed for that evaporation volume. Track if a batch burns by checking if its initial volume was below a minimum safety threshold, storing this as a true or false status. Return the total gallons of syrup produced, the total wood fuel consumed, and a list of indices for the batches that burned.

title: Ice Fishing Safety Assessor
spec: Implement a function assess(lakes) to determine if frozen lakes are safe for use. Each lake provides a base ice thickness and a list of daily average temperatures for the past week. Freezing days incrementally add to the thickness, while days above freezing cause rapid melting that subtracts from it. Calculate the final projected ice thickness for each lake. Compare the final thickness against safety thresholds to determine a true or false status for foot traffic safety and a separate true or false status for snowmobile safety. Output an array of statuses for each lake and the maximum thickness found across all lakes.

title: Roof Thatching Material Calculator
spec: Write a function thatch(roofs) to estimate materials for traditional roof construction. Each roof defines its length, width, pitch angle, and the standard size of a reed bundle. Calculate the base surface area. A steeper pitch angle requires tighter overlapping of the reeds, which acts as a multiplier on the number of bundles needed. Count the total bundles required per roof. Flag a roof with a true or false value if its pitch is too low, meaning water would pool and the design is rejected. Return the total bundles needed for accepted roofs, the estimated labor days, and an array of the rejected roof indices.

title: Cobblestone Street Paving Planner
spec: Create a function pave(streets) to calculate stones and sand for historical street renovations. Each street provides its overall length and width, while standard cobblestones have fixed dimensions and require a specific gap size between them. Calculate the usable area per stone by including one gap width on two sides. Determine the total rows and columns of stones needed to cover each street. Calculate the volume of sand required to fill the gaps based on the street depth. Output the total number of stones required, the total sand volume, and an array of true or false flags indicating if a street is too narrow for standard merchant carts.

title: Bell Ringing Fatigue Simulator
spec: Implement a function ring(sequences) to model a team of bell ringers executing patterns. Inputs include the number of bells, the weight of the heaviest bell, and a list of ringing sequence lengths. Heavier bells cause ringer stamina to drain much faster per strike. Track the stamina pool of the team. For each sequence, calculate the total mathematical permutations rung and subtract the corresponding stamina. If stamina drops below zero during a sequence, mark it as failed using a true or false flag. Output the number of successfully completed sequences, the remaining stamina, and an array of the failed sequence indices.

title: Taffy Pulling Machine Optimizer
spec: Write a function stretch(batches) to process candy manufacturing steps. Each batch has a starting weight, initial temperature, and machine run time in minutes. Every minute on the machine adds a specific number of folds to the candy, which increases its airiness percentage and overall volume. The temperature drops steadily over time; if it falls below a critical threshold before the time is up, the taffy breaks, recorded as a true or false status. Calculate the final volume for each successful batch. Return an array of final volumes, the total weight of broken candy, and a boolean indicating if the machine needs maintenance due to excessive breaks.

title: Bobsled Track Icing Manager
spec: Create a function freeze(segments) to maintain a winter sports track. Each segment provides its length, curve severity, and daily sun exposure percentage. Curves require a thicker baseline ice layer than straightaways. Sunlight melts a percentage of the ice volume each day. Calculate the daily liters of water spray needed to counteract the melting and maintain the minimum required thickness per segment. Keep a true or false flag for any segment that reaches a critical melt rate, requiring sunshades. Return the total water volume needed, the maximum curve severity encountered, and a list of indices for critical segments.

title: Submarine Cable Laying Estimator
spec: Implement a function lay(routes) to calculate underwater infrastructure needs. Each route details the ocean depth, total distance, ship travel speed, and a maximum cable tension limit. Deeper ocean trenches require dropping additional cable slack to prevent snapping. Calculate the total length of cable needed, factoring in the distance and slack. Tension builds if the ship moves too quickly over very deep sections; evaluate if the tension exceeds the safety limit, marking a true or false failure flag if the cable snaps. Return the total cable length used, the accumulated days at sea, and an array of route indices where snapping occurred.

title: Kaleidoscope Symmetry Generator
spec: Write a function generate(scopes) to analyze optical toy configurations. Each scope specifies the number of internal mirrors, the count of glass pieces by color, and an initial rotation degree. The base pattern is formed by the glass pieces, while the number of mirrors multiplies these into reflections. Calculate the total number of visual elements visible in the field of view. Identify the dominant color based on the highest piece count. Determine a true or false status if the configuration forms a perfect mandala, which happens when the rotation degree divides evenly into the mirror count. Output an array of element counts, the dominant colors, and a list of the perfect mandala statuses.

title: Abacus Calculation Simulator
spec: Create a function calculate(operations) to simulate mechanical counting. The input is a list of sequential additions and subtractions. Track the positions of beads in the lower earth deck and upper heaven deck for each decimal column. Moving a bead counts as one mechanical action. When the lower deck exceeds its maximum, carry over a value to the next column and reset the current deck. Maintain a true or false flag if the total value temporarily goes negative, which requires a special borrow state. Output the final numerical result, the total count of mechanical bead movements, and an array showing the final bead counts per column.

title: Matryoshka Doll Nesting Validator
spec: Implement a function nest(dolls) to check wooden doll assembly. The input is a list of dolls, each with an outer diameter and a wood wall thickness. Sort the collection by size. Evaluate if each smaller doll can physically fit inside the next larger one, which requires the smaller doll's outer diameter to be less than the larger doll's outer diameter minus twice its wall thickness. Maintain a true or false status for each attempted insertion. Find the longest unbroken sequence of properly nesting dolls. Return the maximum sequence length, the total weight of the nested set, and an array of the indices of dolls that could not fit anywhere.

title: Sundial Shadow Calibrator
spec: Write a function calibrate(locations) to design timepieces based on the sun. Each location provides its latitude, the height of the central gnomon, and a list of specific solar hours to engrave. Calculate the shadow length and shadow angle for each requested hour using the latitude and gnomon height. Track the maximum shadow length to determine the required radius of the circular dial plate. Determine a true or false flag indicating if the location experiences polar night, where the sun does not rise and no shadows are cast. Return the required plate radius, an array of the calculated angles, and the polar night status.

title: Igloo Construction Forecaster
spec: Create a function build(structures) to simulate arctic shelter building. Each structure request provides a desired inner radius, the local snow density, and the standard snow block dimensions. Calculate the surface area of the dome to determine how many snow blocks are needed. Lower density snow requires thicker blocks for insulation, which reduces the usable inner space. Calculate the total weight of the structure. Evaluate if the total weight exceeds the basal support limit, triggering a true or false collapse flag. Output the total number of blocks needed, the final inner volumes, and an array of collapse flags for each structure.

title: Chocolate Tempering Analyzer
spec: Implement a function temper(batches) to evaluate confectionery processes. Each batch includes its weight and a sequential list of heating and cooling temperatures. Track the formation of cocoa butter crystals as the temperature changes; reaching specific heat points destroys undesirable crystals while holding at lower points builds them. A batch achieves a perfect glossy finish only if the exact target crystal type dominates at the end, recorded as a true or false flag. Calculate the total weight of perfectly tempered chocolate. Return an array of the perfect status flags, the total usable weight, and the number of batches that must be remelted.

title: Pipe Organ Voicing Balancer
spec: Write a function voice(pipes) to calibrate a musical instrument. Each pipe details its length in feet, its material, and its target wind pressure. Calculate the resonant frequency produced by each pipe length. Metal pipes require a higher air pressure multiplier than wooden ones. Accumulate the total air volume required when all pipes play simultaneously. Compare this volume against the instrument's wind chest capacity; if it exceeds the limit, the organ sounds flat, marked by a true or false flag. Output an array of the calculated frequencies, the total air pressure deficit, and the flat sounding status.

title: Windup Toy Mechanism Tester
spec: Create a function wind(toys) to evaluate spring-loaded machines. Each toy has a spring stiffness rating, a number of key turns applied, and its physical weight. The key turns store potential energy based on the stiffness. However, applying too many turns relative to the stiffness breaks the mainspring, marked as a true or false failure status. For surviving toys, calculate the walking distance by dividing the stored energy by the toy's weight. Output the total distance walked by all functional toys, the average walking distance, and an array of indices representing the broken toys.

title: Kelp Forest Harvesting Yield
spec: Implement a function harvest(sectors) to plan ocean farming operations. Each sector provides the current kelp density, the water depth, and the prevailing ocean current speed. Fast currents significantly reduce the efficiency of the cutting blades. Calculate the collected yield per sector by factoring density, depth, and the current penalty. Keep adding the yield to the boat's hold until it reaches maximum capacity, setting a true or false flag when the boat is completely full. Output the total kelp yield collected, the total time spent cutting, and a list of sector indices that were left unharvested.

title: Clock Tower Gear Inspector
spec: Write a function inspect(gears) to evaluate a municipal clock mechanism. Each gear lists its tooth count, a wear percentage, and a true or false flag indicating the presence of rust. Calculate the overall gear ratio from the first to the last gear to find the final dial speed. High wear or rust on critical driver gears causes the teeth to slip, which results in lost time. Count how many gears need immediate replacement because their wear exceeds safety thresholds. Return the estimated daily time lost in minutes, the replacement count, and a boolean indicating if the clock mechanism is completely seized.

title: Chalkboard Dust Accumulation Tracker
spec: Create a function erase(lectures) to model classroom cleaning. Inputs include the board's writing area, the chalk usage rate per minute, and the eraser's dust absorption capacity. Writing consumes chalk and deposits dust onto the board. Erasing removes dust from the board and adds it to the eraser. When the eraser exceeds its capacity, it smears instead of cleaning, marked by a true or false flag, requiring the teacher to clap it outside to reset its capacity. Track the total dust levels. Output the number of clapping events, the final amount of dust left on the board, and an array of smear statuses per lecture.

title: Alpaca Shearing Sorter
spec: Implement a function shear(herd) to process a farm's wool production. Each alpaca provides its age, fleece weight, and a color grading code. First-year alpacas yield a premium softer fleece, which receives a higher market multiplier. Sort and accumulate the total fleece weight into categories based on the color code. If an alpaca was sheared too recently, its fleece weight is too low to harvest, and it is skipped, recorded via a true or false flag. Return an array of total weights by color, the accumulated premium fleece weight, and the count of skipped alpacas.

title: Gondola Lift Operations Simulator
spec: Write a function operate(cabins) to manage a mountain transport system. Each cabin specifies its passenger capacity. The inputs also include the total passenger queue size, the average wind speed, and the operating hours. High winds trigger a true or false safety mode that reduces the running speed of all cabins, increasing the round trip time. Calculate how many round trips each cabin can complete in the given hours. Determine the total number of passengers transported and subtract them from the queue. Output the transported count, the remaining queue size, and an array of trip counts per cabin.

title: Taxidermy Specimen Preservation
spec: Write a function `preserve(specimens, funds)` that evaluates a list of museum taxidermy requests. Each request is a list containing the animal name, its degradation percentage, a flag indicating if it is a rare species, and the preservation cost. Calculate the total cost of all rare species that have a degradation above fifty percent. Also, create a list of names for all specimens that can be fully restored within the given funds, processing them in the order they appear until the funds run out. Return a list containing the total rare repair cost, a boolean indicating if the funds were sufficient to restore every requested item, and the list of restored animal names.

title: Harp String Maintenance
spec: Implement a function `restring(harps)` that processes a list of harp maintenance records. Each record is a list with the harp serial identifier, the number of broken strings, the hours since last tuning, and a true or false flag denoting if it is an antique instrument. A harp requires immediate restringing if it has more than three broken strings, or if it is an antique with over two hundred hours since the last tuning. Calculate the total number of new strings needed across all harps requiring maintenance. Return a list containing the total strings needed, a boolean showing if any antique harp needs maintenance, and a list of the serial identifiers for harps that require restringing.

title: Mushroom Foraging Evaluator
spec: Create a function `forage(mushrooms, threshold)` that filters a collection of gathered fungi. Each mushroom is represented as a list holding the species name, its weight in grams, a toxicity flag, and the cap diameter. A mushroom is considered premium if it is not toxic, weighs more than the specified threshold, and has a cap diameter larger than ten centimeters. Sum the total weight of all premium mushrooms found in the collection. Return a list containing the total premium weight, a boolean indicating if any toxic mushrooms were safely discarded, and a list of the premium species names.

title: Macrame Cord Estimator
spec: Write a function `macrame(patterns, spool)` that determines which wall hangings can be crafted from a single spool of cotton cord. Each pattern is a list containing the design name, the required cord length in meters, the complexity level from one to five, and a flag indicating if it needs wooden beads. A pattern is feasible if its required cord is less than or equal to the remaining spool length and its complexity is under four. Process the patterns sequentially, deducting the required length from the spool for each feasible design. Return a list containing the remaining spool length, a boolean indicating if any designs requiring wooden beads were selected, and a list of the feasible design names.

title: Fossil Excavation Analyzer
spec: Implement a function `excavate(sites, workers)` that plans paleo digs based on available resources. Each site is a list containing the location name, estimated depth in meters, a flag indicating if fragile bones are expected, and the required number of personnel. A site is viable if the required personnel is less than or equal to the available workers and the depth is less than twenty meters. Deduct the required workers for each viable site as you iterate through the list. Return a list comprising the remaining available workers, a boolean indicating if any fragile sites were skipped due to a lack of workers, and a list of the viable location names.

title: Sea Glass Sorter
spec: Create a function `evaluate(fragments, limit)` that sorts washed up glass pieces for jewelry making. Each fragment is a list holding its color, its smoothness rating out of ten, a flag denoting if it has sharp edges, and its size in millimeters. A fragment is suitable if it has no sharp edges, a smoothness rating of at least eight, and a size strictly under the given limit. Tally the number of suitable fragments that are colored blue or green. Return a list containing the total count of suitable blue or green fragments, a boolean denoting if any perfectly smooth fragments with a rating of ten were found, and a list of all suitable fragment colors in the order they were inspected.

title: Shipwreck Salvage Evaluator
spec: Write a function `salvage(artifacts, capacity)` that selects recovered underwater items for preservation. Each artifact is provided as a list containing the item description, its estimated historical value in dollars, its weight in kilograms, and a flag stating if it requires immediate desalination. An artifact is chosen if its weight fits within the remaining lift capacity and its value exceeds five hundred dollars. Subtract the weight of each chosen artifact from the capacity as you process them. Return a list holding the total historical value of the chosen items, a boolean indicating if the lift capacity was completely exhausted to zero, and a list of the chosen item descriptions.

title: Gramophone Stylus Wear
spec: Implement a function `stylus(records, lifespan)` that calculates how many vintage shellac records can be played before the needle needs replacing. Each record is a list with the song title, the playback duration in minutes, the groove condition rating from one to five, and a flag indicating if it is a rare pressing. Playing a record degrades the needle lifespan by its duration, multiplied by two if the groove condition is below three. Stop processing when the lifespan drops below zero. Return a list containing the remaining lifespan, a boolean showing if any rare pressings were played, and a list of the song titles played successfully before the needle wore out.

title: Arm Wrestling Fatigue
spec: Create a function `grapple(matches, stamina)` that simulates an arm wrestler progressing through a tournament. Each match is a list comprising the opponent name, their strength rating, a flag indicating if they use a top roll technique, and the expected match duration in seconds. A match is won if the current stamina is greater than the opponent strength rating. Upon winning, stamina decreases by ten plus the match duration; if the opponent uses a top roll, stamina decreases by an additional five. Return a list containing the final stamina, a boolean indicating if the wrestler went undefeated, and a list of the names of all defeated opponents.

title: Weather Balloon Payload
spec: Write a function `launch(instruments, maximum)` that determines which atmospheric sensors can be attached to a weather balloon. Each instrument is a list with the sensor name, its mass in grams, a flag indicating if it requires a heated casing, and its calibration priority. An instrument is approved if its mass does not exceed the remaining payload capacity and its calibration priority is higher than fifty. Deduct the mass of each approved instrument from the maximum capacity sequentially. Return a list containing the unused payload capacity, a boolean showing if any heated sensors were approved, and a list of the approved sensor names.

title: Bronze Casting Alloy Evaluator
spec: Implement a function `smelt(ingots, temperature)` that processes raw metal additions for a bronze sculpture. Each ingot is a list containing the metal type, its weight in ounces, its melting point, and a flag denoting if it contains impurities. An ingot successfully melts if its melting point is less than or equal to the furnace temperature and it has no impurities. Calculate the total weight of all successfully melted ingots. Return a list containing the total melted weight, a boolean indicating if any impure ingots were rejected from the furnace, and a list of the metal types that successfully melted.

title: Homing Pigeon Navigation
spec: Create a function `navigate(waypoints, energy)` that tracks a racing pigeon along its flight path. Each waypoint is a list holding the landmark name, the distance from the previous point in kilometers, a flag indicating if there is a headwind, and the altitude in meters. The bird consumes one unit of energy per kilometer flown, plus two extra units if flying into a headwind. The flight ends early if the energy drops below zero before reaching a waypoint. Return a list containing the remaining energy, a boolean indicating if the bird encountered any headwinds along its successful legs, and a list of landmark names the bird successfully reached.

title: Mosaic Tile Grouting
spec: Write a function `grout(tiles, cement)` that calculates the coverage of grout across a decorative mosaic. Each tile is a list with the shape name, the gap width in millimeters, a flag denoting if it is a border piece, and the required cement volume in milliliters. A tile is successfully grouted if the available cement is greater than or equal to the required volume and the gap width is under five millimeters. Subtract the required volume for each successfully grouted tile from the available cement. Return a list containing the leftover cement, a boolean indicating if any border pieces were grouted, and a list of the shape names of the grouted tiles.

title: Lace Bobbin Winder
spec: Implement a function `wind(spools, capacity)` that prepares bobbins for lacemaking. Each spool is a list comprising the thread color, the yardage available, a flag indicating if it is a metallic thread, and the thread thickness rating. A spool is wound onto a bobbin if its thickness rating is less than three and its available yardage can completely fill the bobbin capacity. Deduct the bobbin capacity from the spool yardage for each successful wind. Count the total number of bobbins successfully prepared. Return a list containing the total bobbins wound, a boolean showing if any metallic threads were processed, and a list of the colors of the wound threads.

title: Sword Engraving Estimator
spec: Create a function `engrave(requests, stamina)` that evaluates customized etchings on replica swords. Each request is a list containing the customer name, the number of characters to engrave, a flag indicating if they requested gold inlay, and the complexity score. Engraving consumes stamina equal to the number of characters multiplied by the complexity score. A request is completed if the artisan has enough stamina remaining. Deduct the required stamina for each completed request sequentially. Return a list containing the artisan remaining stamina, a boolean indicating if any completed requests included gold inlay, and a list of the customer names whose requests were completed.

title: Astrolabe Star Alignment
spec: Write a function `align(stars, visibility)` that filters celestial bodies for ancient navigation. Each star is a list holding the constellation name, its brightness magnitude, a flag indicating if it is a pole star, and its elevation angle. A star is usable if its brightness is greater than the visibility threshold and its elevation is above ten degrees. Sum the total elevation of all usable stars found in the sky. Return a list containing the total usable elevation, a boolean denoting if a pole star was found among the usable ones, and a list of the constellation names of the usable stars.

title: Marionette Control Inspector
spec: Implement a function `inspect(strings, tolerance)` that evaluates the control lines of a wooden marionette. Each string is a list with the body part name, the current tension in newtons, a flag indicating if it is tangled, and the target tension. A string requires adjustment if it is tangled or if the absolute difference between the current and target tension exceeds the tolerance limit. Count the total number of strings requiring adjustment. Return a list containing the total adjustment count, a boolean showing if any tangled strings were found, and a list of the body part names that must be fixed.

title: Neon Tube Bending
spec: Create a function `bend(tubes, heat)` that determines which glass sections can be shaped for a neon sign. Each tube is a list comprising the gas color, the length in inches, a flag indicating if it requires a sharp angle, and the necessary softening temperature. A tube can be bent if its softening temperature is less than or equal to the current heat and its length is under forty inches. If a tube requires a sharp angle, the available heat drops by five units immediately after bending. Return a list containing the final remaining heat, a boolean indicating if any tubes requiring sharp angles were successfully bent, and a list of the gas colors of the bent tubes.
